items.title: Needs
items.text:
What the player needs to live: hunger, thirst, tiredness, or whatever the game wants. Each need goes down over time; at zero, the player loses health. It goes back up by eating or drinking what the inventory holds, at a source in the world (a well, a bed) carrying this system, or through a Trigger rule. Each need can be switched off without losing its settings.

Identifier besoins Version 3 Placed on objects yes Also activates Health Also needs, on the same object Interaction

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Game tab, Systems section, by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices The player's needs One row per need, with its name, its reserve, what it loses per minute and what happens at zero. Hunger and thirst by default; add tiredness, cold, or remove what your game does not want. Untick "On" to switch a need off without losing its settings. besoins List of “Need” [{'nom': 'Faim', 'actif': True, 'max': 100, 'baisse': 2, 'course': 0, 'degats': 1, 'vide': 'rien', 'couleur': '#d9893b'}, {'nom': 'Soif', 'actif': True, 'max': 100, 'baisse': 3, 'course': 1, 'degats': 1, 'vide': 'rien', 'couleur': '#3b9ad9'}] one line per “Need”: its fields What can be eaten and drunk The inventory items that raise a need when the player uses them up: a click on their slot in the inventory window. One item can have several rows: a watermelon feeds and quenches. aliments List of “Food” (empty) one line per “Food”: its fields A click in the inventory uses up a food Ticked: in the inventory window (I), a click on a food's slot eats or drinks it. Unticked: only through the event besoins.consommer, from a script or a Trigger rule. manger_fenetre Yes or no yes Use nothing up when the need is full Ticked: a food whose needs are all full is not eaten, and does not disappear for nothing. rien_si_plein Yes or no yes Warning level (%) Below this share of the reserve, the bar blinks and the need is announced (besoins.bas): a sound, a message. 0: never a warning. alerte Number 25 from 0 to 100 Health regained per second, when satisfied The health points the player regains each second while all their needs are above the level below: well fed, they heal. 0: never. soin_rassasie Number 0 from 0 to 100 000 Satisfied above (%) The share of their reserve that every need must be above for the player to regain health. seuil_rassasie Number 80 from 0 to 100 Player speed when a need slows them down The share of their usual speed the player keeps while a need set to "walks slower" is at zero: 0.6 keeps 60 %. lenteur Number 0.6 from 0.1 to 1 Show the bars Shows one bar per need on screen, with its name, under the health bar. Untick it if your game shows them its own way (a drawn screen, with besoins.change). afficher Yes or no yes Horizontal position (0 to 1) Where the bars start, from left to right: 0 at the left edge of the screen, 1 at the right edge. 0.02 lines them up with the health bar. x Number 0.02 from 0 to 1 Vertical position of the first (0 to 1) Where the first bar sits, from top to bottom: 0 at the top of the screen, 1 at the bottom. The next ones line up under it. y Number 0.1 from 0 to 1 Width (share of the screen) The length of a full bar, as a share of the screen width. largeur Number 0.18 from 0.02 to 1 Height (share of the screen) The thickness of a bar, as a share of the screen height. hauteur Number 0.014 from 0.005 to 0.2 Gap between two bars The distance from one bar to the next, as a share of the screen height. ecart Number 0.03 from 0.005 to 0.3

items.title: The fields of each “Need”
items.text:
In the Properties, each “Need” has its own numbered frame; Add: Need adds one, the cross removes it. A field only appears when it is useful: under its name, the table says when.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Name The name the player sees next to its bar, such as "Hunger", "Thirst" or "Tiredness". Foods and sources name it exactly as written here. nom Text (empty) On Ticked: the need counts in the game. Unticked: it is switched off, without losing its settings: no bar, it does not go down and never hurts; the foods and sources that raise it do nothing (the prompt says so, the food stays in the inventory). To try the game without tiredness, for example. actif Yes or no yes Full reserve The value of the need when the player is satisfied, at the start of the game. Losses and what foods give are compared with it: with 100 and a loss of 2 per minute, it takes 50 minutes to reach zero. max Number 100 from 1 to 100 000 Loss per minute What the need loses per minute of play, standing still or walking. 0: it never goes down by itself (tiredness that only comes from running). baisse Number 2 from 0 to 100 000 Extra loss while running (per minute) What the need loses on top per minute of running: running makes one thirsty and tired. 0: running changes nothing. course Number 0 from 0 to 100 000 Health lost per second at zero The health points the player loses each second while this need is at zero. 0: it does not kill, only the effect chosen below. degats Number 1 from 0 to 100 000 At zero, also What also happens while the need is at zero, until it goes back up: nothing, a slower walk (hunger), or no more running or jumping (tiredness). vide Choice in a list Nothing more rien: Nothing morelent: The player walks slowersans_course: The player can no longer run or jump Color of its bar The color of this need's bar on screen: orange for hunger, blue for thirst, purple for tiredness. couleur Color #d9893b

items.title: The fields of each “Food”
items.text:
In the Properties, each “Food” has its own numbered frame; Add: Food adds one, the cross removes it. A field only appears when it is useful: under its name, the table says when.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Item (kind of inventory item) The kind of item used up, as the inventory stores it, such as "Apple", "Flask" or "Cooked meat". One goes each time. objet Text (empty) Need raised (its name) The name of the need it raises, written as in the list of needs: "Hunger" or "Thirst". besoin Text (empty) By how much What it gives back to the need, without going past the full reserve: 30 out of 100 for an apple, 60 for a meal. montant Number 30 from 0 to 100 000 Health given too The health points it also gives back, like a hot meal. 0: only the need. vie Number 0 from 0 to 100 000

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Need raised when used (its name) An object of the world carrying this system raises this need when the player uses it (E): "Thirst" for a well or a river, "Tiredness" for a bed. Written as in the list of needs. source_besoin Text (empty) By how much, each use What one use gives back to the need, without going past the full reserve: 100 fills it all. source_montant Number 100 from 0 to 100 000 Prompt text (Drink, Sleep… empty: Interaction's) The word of the prompt in front of the source, such as "Drink" or "Sleep". Empty: the usual text of the Interaction system. source_verbe Text (empty) Wait between two uses (s) The time, in seconds of play, before the source works again: a well that fills up, a bed one cannot use again at once. 0: always ready. source_recharge Number 0 from 0 to 86 400 Hours that pass when used (Day and night system) With the Day and night system, using it moves the clock on that much: 8 for a night in a bed. 0: time does not jump. source_heures Number 0 from 0 to 24

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description besoins.change besoin (text), valeur (number), max (number) A need of the player (hunger, thirst, tiredness...) changed by a whole point, or is announced once when the game starts. besoin is its name as written in the needs list (original language). besoins.bas besoin (text), valeur (number), max (number) A need went below the warning level of the besoins system (its bar blinks): a sound, a message, a quest hint. besoins.vide besoin (text) A need reached zero: from now on the player loses health each second (and maybe walks slower or cannot run), until it goes back up. besoins.consomme objet (text) The player ate or drank one item of the inventory (its foods list): it has been taken from the inventory and its needs raised. besoins.source cible (id), besoin (text), montant (number) The player used a source of the world carrying the besoins system (a well, a river, a bed): besoin went up by montant. sante.blesser cible (id), montant (number), source (id?) Ask the health module to remove health from an object. sante.soigner cible (id), montant (number) Ask the health module to give health back, up to its maximum. inventaire.retirer objet (text), quantite (number) Ask the inventory to remove items, such as a payment. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.manque if there are not enough. jour_nuit.avancer heures (number) Ask the day and night system to move the clock on by heures (a night in a bed: 8). Every hour, sunrise and sunset crossed are announced in order.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description besoins.remplir besoin (text), montant (number) Ask the besoins system to raise a need by its name, without using anything up: a meal at an inn, a Trigger rule, a script. besoins.consommer objet (text) Ask the besoins system to eat or drink one item of the inventory, as a click on its slot would: nothing happens if it is not a food or the player has none. inventaire.change objet (text), quantite (number), total (number), chargement (boolean?) The quantity of an item changed. total is the new quantity. chargement is true when a saved game gives the items back (game.load): nothing was picked up. inventaire.choisi objet (text), total (number) The player clicked a slot of the inventory window: objet is the kind of item, total how many they carry. What it does belongs to the game: eat, equip, read. interaction.utiliser cible (id), joueur (id) The player used the object in reach: a door, a merchant, an item to pick up. Whoever owns that object decides what it does. sante.change cible (id), vie (number), max (number) An object's health changed, or is announced once when the game starts. langue.change langue (text) Sent by the engine when the player changes the game's language (game.set_language, the Menu options). A module redraws what it already shows: its texts go through game.t and game.language.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • besoins.baisse: function(default, besoin, par_minute) -> how much this need goes down per minute right now (number). The default is its baisse setting, plus its course setting while the player runs. To make thirst fall faster in the desert or at noon, hunger slower while sleeping.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Needs (besoins)
items.text:
Hunger, thirst, tiredness, or any need the game wants: each one goes down with the time of play, and at zero the player loses health. Add it once with modules_add (it needs sante: put sante on the player, and barre_de_vie to show the health). Use it whenever the user talks about eating, drinking, starving, sleeping or survival: never write a hunger script.

  • The needs (game setting besoins, modules_set): a list, one row per need, in the user's language. Hunger and thirst by default; add « Fatigue » or anything else, remove what the user did not ask for. Each row: nom (shown next to its bar, and how foods and sources name it), actif (true by default; false switches the need off without losing its settings: no bar, it does not fall, never hurts, and its foods and sources do nothing, saying so; a row without it is on), max (the full reserve, the value at the start), baisse (lost per minute of play), course (lost on top per minute of running), degats (health lost per second at zero; 0: it never kills), vide (also at zero: rien, lent (the player walks at lenteur of their speed), sans_course (no running nor jumping: tiredness)), couleur (its bar).
  • Tiredness (« Fatigue ») is a row of its own, like hunger: add it only when the user wants sleep to matter (baisse low or 0, course for running, vide sans_course, degats 0 so it never kills), and set actif false when they want to try the game without it, rather than deleting the row. Ask, or offer, how energy comes back; any mix works: sleep in a bed (a source: source_besoin « Fatigue », source_verbe « Dormir », source_heures 8 with jour_nuit), a food or drink (an aliments row: « Café », besoin « Fatigue »), or anything else through a declencheur rule with the action remplir_besoin (besoin « Fatigue », montant): resting by a campfire (a zone around it, quand entree, fois chaque), sitting on a bench (quand utilise), a prayer at an altar. Never a script for that.
  • Foods (game setting aliments): which inventory items raise which need, by how much (objet, besoin written as the need's nom, montant), and vie (health given too). One row per need an item raises: a watermelon feeds and quenches. The player eats with a click on its slot in the inventory window (I), as long as manger_fenetre is on; rien_si_plein keeps a food when its needs are full. The items themselves come from inventaire (picked up), collecte (gathered: berries from a bush), fabrication (cooked at a campfire) or boutique.
  • Sources in the world: place besoins on an object (systems_attach; interaction comes with it) and set source_besoin (the need's nom), source_montant, source_verbe (the prompt: « Boire », « Dormir »), source_recharge (seconds before it works again), source_heures (hours that pass, with jour_nuit: 8 for a bed). A well, a river bank, a bed, a spring.
  • Dosage: with baisse 2 per minute and max 100, hunger reaches zero after 50 minutes of play. Say the numbers to the user and check them with game_run (a long segment doing nothing): the player must have time to find food, and doing nothing must end badly if the user asked for a survival game.
  • Game settings: alerte (% under which the bar blinks and besoins.bas is sent), soin_rassasie and seuil_rassasie (health regained per second while every need is above that %), afficher and the bars' place (x, y, largeur, hauteur, ecart: they line up under the health bar by default).
  • Events announced: besoins.change (besoin, valeur, max), besoins.bas, besoins.vide (besoin), besoins.consomme (objet), besoins.source (cible, besoin, montant). Send besoins.remplir (besoin, montant) to raise a need without using anything (a meal at an inn; from a declencheur rule, use its action remplir_besoin, which sends it with these fields), besoins.consommer (objet) to eat an item from a script or a declencheur rule.
  • Change how fast a need falls from your own script, never the module's: game.override("besoins.baisse", function(default, besoin, par_minute) if besoin == "Soif" and game.has_tag(game.ground(game.player()) or "", "desert") then return par_minute * 2 end return default(besoin, par_minute) end).
  • Saved games: game.save keeps every need and the sources' waiting time; game.load gives them back. Nothing to write.
  • HUD keys start with besoins.: do not use that prefix in a game script. The bars are numbered among the needs that are on: besoins.1 is the first bar shown.
  • Testing: in game_run, read the report's hud (besoins.1, besoins.1.nom...) and the besoins.* events; a script listening to sante.change shows the health lost at zero.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One copy per player: each player has their own needs, bars, food and penalties; a source (a well, a bed) refills the player who uses it. A bed that moves the clock on (jour_nuit.avancer) moves it on for everyone: the day is shared.

In the Game tab, Systems section, by opening the system's card.

The player picks it up or receives it like any item. monnaie Text Or Opens when the player uses it (E) Ticked: the shop opens when the player uses the merchant. If they also carry a Dialogue, they talk first, and their last line offers "Show me your goods". Unticked: only through the event boutique.ouvrir, from a zone or a script. a_l_usage Yes or no yes What they sell The shop's items, in the order they show: the kind of item, how many one purchase gives, the price, the stock, and what the merchant pays if the player sells one to them. articles List of “Item” (empty) one line per “Item”: its fields

items.title: The fields of each “Item”
items.text:
In the Properties, each “Item” has its own numbered frame; Add: Item adds one, the cross removes it. A field only appears when it is useful: under its name, the table says when.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Item (kind of inventory item) The kind of item sold, as the inventory stores it, such as "Sword" or "Apple". Items of the same kind add up in the inventory. objet Text (empty) They sell it Ticked: the item can be bought, with a Buy button. Unticked: the merchant only buys it back (then set the buy-back), like wolf pelts they collect. a_vendre Yes or no yes How many per purchase How many one purchase gives: 10 for a quiver of 10 arrows. quantite Number 1 from 1 to 1 000 000, as a whole number Price How much money one purchase costs. 0: it is free. prix Number 10 from 0 to 1 000 000, as a whole number Stock at the start (0: no limit) How many purchases of this item the merchant can make before running out: 1 for a unique sword. 0: they never run out. What the player sells back to them adds to it. stock Number 0 from 0 to 1 000 000, as a whole number Buy-back: what they pay for one (0: they buy none) The price the merchant pays when the player sells them one of this item: a Sell button appears. 0: they buy none, and nothing shows. rachat Number 0 from 0 to 1 000 000, as a whole number

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description boutique.achat cible (id), objet (text), quantite (number), prix (number), monnaie (text) The player bought an item in a shop: cible is the merchant, quantite how many they received, prix what they paid, in monnaie (a kind of inventory item). The inventory has already changed. boutique.vente cible (id), objet (text), quantite (number), prix (number), monnaie (text) The player sold an item to a merchant (cible): quantite how many they gave, prix what they received, in monnaie. The inventory has already changed. inventaire.ajouter objet (text), quantite (number), joueur (id?) Ask the inventory to add items, such as a reward. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.plein. With several players, joueur says whose bag; without it, the player whose action is being handled, or every player. inventaire.retirer objet (text), quantite (number) Ask the inventory to remove items, such as a payment. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.manque if there are not enough.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description interaction.utiliser cible (id), joueur (id) The player used the object in reach: a door, a merchant, an item to pick up. Whoever owns that object decides what it does. boutique.ouvrir cible (id) Ask the shop system to open the shop of cible, as if the player had used it: from a dialogue answer, a trigger, a script. inventaire.change objet (text), quantite (number), total (number), chargement (boolean?) The quantity of an item changed. total is the new quantity. chargement is true when a saved game gives the items back (game.load): nothing was picked up. inventaire.plein objet (text) An item could not be added: every slot holds another kind of item. inventaire.manque objet (text), quantite (number) Items could not be removed: there are not enough. hud.clic cible (text), joueur (id?) A button of the HUD was clicked: pressed, then released on it; or chosen with A (Enter) while it has the gamepad or keyboard focus; or the window's back button (back = true), with B (Escape). cible is the button's key (game.hud_button), joueur the player who clicked (a guest clicks on their own computer; the host plays the click). Announced by the engine, before the scripts' on_update of that step.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • boutique.texte: function(default, key) -> the text the shop shows for that key: titre_vide, bourse, acheter, vendre, prix, reste, epuise, plus_en_stock, fermer, achete, vendu, manque, place, sans_objet. It may hold {objet}, {n} and {monnaie}, replaced afterwards (the item and the money in the player's language). The default is the game's translation of the text in the original language (translations_get lists them as built-in texts of the shop); without one, French or English, after the player's language.

items.title: Shop (boutique)
items.text:
A merchant who sells: when the player uses them (E), a window lists their items with prices, the player's money, and Buy and Sell buttons. The money is a kind of inventory item, such as "Or". Activating it activates interaction and inventaire; placing it on an object places interaction there too. Use it for every shop the user asks for (a merchant, a blacksmith, a vending machine) rather than a script.

Place it on the merchant with systems_attach, then set its values with systems_set:

  • articles: the list of what they sell, one row each: objet (the kind of item, as the inventory stores it: "Épée"), a_vendre (on: it can be bought; off: the merchant only buys it back), quantite (how many one purchase gives: 10 arrows), prix, stock (purchases before running out; 0: no limit), rachat (what the merchant pays when the player sells one back; 0: they buy none, and no Sell button shows).
  • monnaie: the kind of item used to pay ("Or" by default). Name it, and the items, in the user's language, exactly as the inventory stores them. The player gets money like any item: coins to pick up (inventaire with quantite 50), a quest reward, inventaire.ajouter.
  • nom: the window's title (empty: the object's name). Set the interaction prompt texte to "Shop" or "Trade" in the user's language.
  • a_l_usage (on by default): the shop opens when the merchant is used. A merchant who also carries dialogue talks first, and nothing has to be turned off: the shop waits, and the dialogue's last line offers a "Show me your goods" button ("Voir la marchandise" in French) that closes the conversation and opens the shop. To offer it elsewhere in the conversation, give an answer annonce: "boutique.ouvrir" and suite: "fin" (the answer's event carries the merchant as cible): the dialogue then adds no button of its own. Turn a_l_usage off only for a shop opened by a zone or a script.

Buying takes the price (inventaire.retirer), then gives the item (inventaire.ajouter). The window says it clearly when the player lacks money ("You need 5 more Gold"), when the inventory is full (they get their money back), or when an item is sold out. Selling does the reverse, one item at a time, and refills a limited stock.

Example, a blacksmith who sells a unique sword and potions, and buys back wolf pelts:

{"monnaie": "Or", "articles": [{"objet": "Épée", "prix": 30, "stock": 1}, {"objet": "Potion", "quantite": 2, "prix": 5}, {"objet": "Peau de loup", "a_vendre": false, "rachat": 4}]}.

Other details:

  • Events: boutique.achat and boutique.vente (cible the merchant, objet, quantite, prix, monnaie), after the inventory changed: for a sound, a quest step ("buy a sword": a quetes step on boutique.achat), a declencheur rule. game.emit("boutique.ouvrir", {cible = id}) opens a merchant's shop from a zone or a script.
  • Game settings: pause (the world stops while shopping, on by default), largeur (the window's width, a share of the screen).
  • Texts follow the player's language. The shop's own texts (Buy, Close...) are built-in texts of the system, listed by translations_get with the game's texts: translate them there for every language the game offers (French and English are built in). The shop's name (nom), the money and the items are translated with the game's tables too; events keep their original names. To change a word, override boutique.texte from a game script: game.override("boutique.texte", function(default, key) if key == "acheter" then return "Prendre" end return default(key) end). Keys and their {n}, {objet}, {monnaie} placeholders are in modules_info.
  • HUD keys start with boutique.: do not use that prefix in a game script.
  • Saved games: game.save keeps what each merchant has left of a limited stock, and game.load gives it back. Nothing to write.
  • Gamepad and keyboard: the first Buy button has the focus; the d-pad or the arrows move it, A or Enter buys, B or Escape closes (boutique.fermer is the window's back button).
  • Testing: in game_run, give money first (inventaire.ajouter), walk to the merchant, press interact, then click boutique.acheter.<row> (or boutique.vendre.<row>, boutique.fermer); the report's hud gives each button's area and boutique.message what the shop answered. With a gamepad: segments with pad (["pad_down"], then ["pad_a"], each followed by a segment without); the report marks the button with the focus (focused).

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One copy per player: each player has their own window and money (their own inventory). A merchant's limited stocks are shared: what one buys is gone for the others. The host's saved game keeps the stocks.

items.title: Fog volume
items.text:
A local fog, limited to an area: the mist of a valley, an undergrowth, a marsh, the smoke of a cave. Create > Fog volume places an invisible box that carries it: it fills the box (or the sphere inside it) and fades out towards its edges. With volumetric fog (High or Medium quality), it catches the sun's rays and shadows. Its kind "Glowing air (rays only)" (Create > Glowing air) is an almost invisible air that only shows the sun's rays, like the dust of a forest.

Identifier brouillard Version 1 Placed on objects yes Run by the engine yes: the engine runs it itself, without a script

Glowing air: an almost invisible air that only shows the sun's rays where they cross it, like dust in a forest or a room. It needs volumetric fog (Sky and light), in High or Medium quality, and a sun that passes between foliage or walls. sorte Choice in a list Fog brouillard: Fogair_lumineux: Glowing air (rays only) Shape Box: the fog fills the object's whole box (a valley, a room). Outside the rays, the air hardly veils anything. distance_air Number 200 from 20 to 2000 Soft edgesshown only if Kind is “Glowing air (rays only)” The part of the box, from its edges, where the air fades out: 1 by default, the rays appear and fade gently, without showing the box's faces. bords_air Number 1 from 0 to 1 Soft edgesshown only if Kind is “Fog” The part of the box, from its edges, where the fog fades out: 0 cuts sharply at the faces, 1 leaves only the core thick. bords Number 0.3 from 0 to 1 Thicker at the bottom 0: the same over the whole height. 1: thick at the bottom of the box, nothing at the top, like a mist that stays on the ground. degrade Number 0 from 0 to 1

items.title: Fog volume (brouillard)
items.text:
An object carrying this system fills its box with a local fog: the mist of a valley or an undergrowth, a marsh, the smoke of a cave, a cloud of dust. The scene fog (world_set fogDistance) covers the whole map; a fog volume stays where you put it. The system has no script: the renderer draws it. Several volumes can overlap: their fog adds up.

  • Make one: create a box (builtin:cube) with visible: false and no collider, then systems_attach this system on it. Scale the box to the area (20 × 6 × 30 for a valley floor, 4 × 3 × 4 for a room): the fog fills it, or the ball inside it (forme "sphere"). Place it so that its bottom is a little under the ground.
  • Per object (systems_set): forme (boite, sphere), distance (m: at this distance inside the fog, 95% is hidden; 5 to 15 for a thick mist, 40 to 100 for a haze; the box must be larger than this distance to hide everything behind it), couleur ("#rrggbb", its color in full light), bords (0 to 1: how much of the box, from its edges, fades out), degrade (0 to 1: 1 is thick at the bottom and nothing at the top, a mist that stays on the ground).
  • With volumetric fog on (world_set volumetricFog true, and High or Medium quality), the volume catches the sun's rays and the shadows of the trees: a fog volume in a forest shows sun shafts there only, without fogging the rest of the map. Raise volumetricAir for brighter shafts.
  • Two kinds (sorte): brouillard (the default, a visible fog) and air_lumineux ("Glowing air (rays only)"), an almost invisible air that only shows the sun's rays where they cross it, like dust in a forest. Pick by what the user describes: "sun rays in the forest", "light shafts", "god rays through the trees or a window", "dust in the light" -> air_lumineux; "mist in the valley", "a foggy marsh", "smoke in a cave", "the forest is misty" -> brouillard. The air has its own settings: distance_air (m, 200 by default; 100 for strong rays, 400 for a light trace) and bords_air (1 by default, keep it); distance, couleur and bords do not apply to it (it has no colour: it takes the sun's). It needs volumetric fog on (world_set volumetricFog true; turn it on if it is off) and a sun low enough to pass between trees or walls; on Low quality it does not show at all. Make its box large and tall enough to hold the rays from the treetops to the ground (30 × 12 × 30 for a clearing). Keep fogDistance 0 if the user wants no mist.
  • In Low quality (and on a small graphics card), it is still drawn, without shadows or rays. Far from the camera it is also drawn without shadows: it never stops at a distance.
  • Do not make its box visible: that would show the box. It moves with its object (a cloud that drifts, smoke that follows a fire).

The engine draws it once for the whole game: every player sees it.

items.title: Map
items.text:
A minimap in a corner of the screen, the player in the middle, and a big map of the whole scene with the M key, zoomed and moved with the mouse or the gamepad (triggers and stick). What carries this system shows on it as a marker: a shape and a color, or an image, and its name; always, once discovered up close, or only as a quest objective. Merchants, characters who talk and the objectives of quests in progress are marked by themselves.

Identifier carte Version 6 Placed on objects yes

In the Game tab, Systems section, by opening the system's card.

It hides during a pause (a menu, a dialogue). mini_carte Yes or no yes Corner of the minimap The corner of the screen where the minimap sits. items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • carte.texte: function(default, key) -> the text the map shows for that key: titre, fermer, aide, decouvert, vous. It may hold {nom}, replaced afterwards. The default is the game's translation of the text in the original language (a built-in text of the map in translations_get); without one, French or English, after the player's language.

items.title: Map (carte)
items.text:
A minimap in a corner of the screen, the player in the middle as an arrow, and a big map of the whole scene opened with the control carte (M, or ↓ on a gamepad), zoomed with the mouse wheel or with the controls carte_rapprocher (Page Up, or the right trigger RT on a gamepad) and carte_eloigner (Page Down, or the left trigger LT), held, and moved by dragging with the mouse, with the gamepad's left stick or with the walking keys. While the map has the gamepad's focus the player does not move, so LT (also run) does not make them run. Add it with modules_add when the user asks for a map, a minimap, markers or places to discover: do not build a map yourself.

The picture is the scene seen from above, taken by the engine when the scene starts (north, -Z, at the top), without the player and characters. The game setting dessin can give a drawn map instead (an image file): by default it covers the same square as the engine's view (dessin_zone "auto"); with dessin_zone "manuelle", dessin_x, dessin_z (its north-west corner) and dessin_cote (its side, in metres) say where it lies.

Markers, without code: place the system on an object (systems_attach), at its position, or on a group or folder: one marker for everything inside, sub-folders included, in the middle of the box enclosing its pieces (the folder's own position does not matter), discovered when the player comes within distance of that box. A piece inside with its own values for carte (systems_set on it) becomes its own marker. Its object settings:

  • nom: the name shown under it on the big map; empty, the name of the object or group without a trailing number. Write it in the user's language.
  • forme: rond, losange, triangle, carre, etoile, or image with image (an icon file, find one with assets_search and kind "image"); couleur ("#rrggbb", tints an image); taille (1 usual, up to 3).
  • visible: toujours; decouvert, shown once the player came within distance metres, or when your script or a declencheur rule sends carte.reveler {cible = id} (the object or group, or any piece of the group); cache, shown only while it is a quest objective.
  • quete and quete_etape: the exact title of a quetes quest (and a step number, 0 for the whole quest) for which this marker is the objective, such as the miller for "Go back to the miller".

What marks itself (game settings marchands and personnages, on by default): objects carrying boutique (a golden diamond) and dialogue (a light blue circle), named after the shop or the character, one marker per object or group they are placed on. Placing carte on one of them chooses its look instead.

Quest objectives (game setting objectifs, couleur_objectif): while a quetes step is active, the markers it names are ringed in that color, and on the minimap they stay at its edge, pointing the way. A step names objects through fin_cible (the "Loup" of "Vaincre 3 loups": every marker on an object or group named "Loup", "Loup 2"...), or a marker names its quest with quete. The quest log is not changed: the map only listens to quetes.debut, quetes.etape and quetes.fin.

Other game settings: mini_carte (shown or not), mini_coin (bas_droite by default, bas_gauche, haut_droite, haut_gauche; the inventory and the current quest step are at the top right), mini_taille (share of the screen height), mini_forme (ronde or carree), mini_etendue (metres shown from edge to edge), mini_tourne (turns with the player, otherwise north up), grande_carte (the M window), pause_fenetre (the world stops while it is open), noms (names on the big map), annoncer (a message when a marker is discovered).

  • Events announced: carte.ouverte (ouvert), carte.decouvert (cible: the object or group the system is placed on, once for all its pieces). Listened: carte.reveler (cible).
  • The minimap hides during a pause (a menu, a dialogue, a shop) and while the big map is open.
  • Saved games keep the places already discovered, in every scene (on_save, on_load): a loaded game shows them again without announcing them.
  • Texts follow the player's language: the map's own texts are built-in texts of the system, listed by translations_get (French and English are built in). To change a word, override carte.texte from a game script: game.override("carte.texte", function(default, key) if key == "titre" then return "Atlas" end return default(key) end). Keys: titre, fermer, aide, decouvert (with {nom}), vous.
  • When the world changes a lot (a bridge built, a forest burnt), game.map_refresh() from a script takes the picture again.
  • HUD keys start with carte.: do not use that prefix in a game script.
  • Testing: in game_run, read the report's hud: carte.mini.r.<n> are the minimap markers, carte.mini.o.<n> the rings of objectives, carte.mini.joueur the arrow; press carte and read carte.g.n.<n> (the names on the big map) and carte.grande.image (its uv, the part of the map shown). wheel and mouse in a segment zoom and drag it, stick ([x, y], y down) moves it, actions carte_rapprocher or carte_eloigner held zoom it in or out. A discovery sends carte.decouvert, counted in the report's events.
  • Not yet: a fog of war (the parts of the map not yet walked hidden in black).

items.text:
One copy per player: each player has their own minimap, map window and discovered places.

items.title: Ragdoll
items.text:
An animated character that falls limp, like a rag doll: when it dies, under a hard hit, or when the Trigger asks. Its body is built on its own, from its skeleton. It can get back up, and its animation resumes smoothly.

Identifier chiffon Version 2 Placed on objects yes

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Game tab, Systems section, by opening the system's card.

None.

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Falls limp when it dies (Health system) When its health reaches zero, it collapses like a rag doll, and does not get back up. a_la_mort Yes or no yes Falls under a hit harder than (m/s, 0: never) An object that hits it and gives it more than this speed, in meters per second, knocks it down: a rolling rock, a thrown barrel. 6: a clear hit. 0: never. choc Number 6 from 0 to 100 Gets back up after a hit Knocked down by a hit (not by dying), it gets back up after a while, and its animation resumes smoothly. se_relever Yes or no yes Gets up after (s) How many seconds it stays down before getting up, once still. delai Number 3 from 0.2 to 60 Mass (kg) The weight of the falling body, in kilograms, shared among its limbs by their size: 70 for an adult, 25 for a child, 300 for an ogre. masse Number 70 from 1 to 10 000 Limb looseness (degrees) How far each limb can bend relative to the one carrying it, in degrees: 45 is natural, 20 falls stiff like a statue, 90 is very floppy. raideur Number 45 from 5 to 120 Floats in water Fallen into water, the body floats, the head and shoulders just above the water, and drifts with it. Otherwise, it sinks slowly to the bottom, like a knight in armor. flotte Yes or no yes

items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description chiffon.tombe cible (id) A character fell limp as a ragdoll: on its death, under a hard hit, or by game.ragdoll. Announced by the engine. chiffon.releve cible (id) A ragdoll got back up: its animation resumes. Announced by the engine.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description sante.mort cible (id), source (id?) An object's health reached zero. What happens next belongs to the game: the health module does nothing else, unless its setting says to destroy the object.

items.title: Ragdoll (chiffon)
items.text:
An animated character falls limp like a rag doll, then can get back up and its animation resumes smoothly. Its body is built by the engine from its skeleton (capsules measured on its bones, joints with reasonable limits): nothing to set per model, any skeleton works.

  • systems_attach it on the characters (the player, enemies, villagers) or their folder. Per object: a_la_mort (falls when its sante reaches zero, and stays down), choc (a hit from a moving object faster than this, in m/s, knocks it down; 0 never), se_relever and delai (after a hit, it gets back up once still for that many seconds), masse (kg), raideur (how far each limb bends, in degrees: 45 natural, 20 stiff).
  • In water, the fallen body floats, head and shoulders just above the surface, and drifts; set « flotte » to false to make it sink (a knight in armor). The game_run « water » part lists it.
  • The character must be animated (a model with bones and animations): a static model cannot fall as a ragdoll.
  • Without code: a declencheur rule with action chiffon (falls) or relever (gets up), cible the character.
  • Scripts: game.ragdoll(id, true) makes it fall (an optional third argument, a vec, throws it), game.ragdoll(id, false) gets it back up, game.ragdolled(id) tells if it is down. Events chiffon.tombe and chiffon.releve (cible).
  • While down, the player does not move and the camera follows the body; a character is not walked by its scripts.
  • Check with game_run: ragdolls gives each one's falls, get_ups, and whether it is down at the end.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One for the whole game: any character carrying it falls on death, guests' characters included (on the host; guests see their place, not the limp pose).

items.title: Gathering
items.text:
What carries this system is a resource to gather: a tree to chop, a rock to mine, a bush to pick. Each use is a hit; at the last one, the resource gives what it holds to the inventory, disappears, and grows back if wanted.

Identifier collecte Version 8 Placed on objects yes Also activates Interaction Also needs, on the same object Interaction

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Game tab, Systems section, by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Show what is gathered on screen Briefly writes on screen what the player has just gathered ("+3 Wood"), and the message when the tool is missing. Untick it if your game shows this its own way. afficher Yes or no yes Chips at each hit At each hit, a few chips jump from the spot hit, in its colour: wood for a tree's trunk, stone for a rock. Untick it for a game without particles. eclats Yes or no yes Gather what needs a tool with The attack (the default), as in survival games: the player holds the axe in hand (the inventory's bar) and strikes the tree with the left click. The interaction: the E key gathers, having the tool in the bag is enough, as before. What is gathered bare-handed (berries) stays on the interaction. recolte_outil Choice in a list The attack, with the tool held in hand attaque: The attack, with the tool held in handinteraction: The interaction (E), with the tool in the bag Attack action that gathers The game's control action that strikes a resource with the tool in hand ("attack": the left click by default, X on a gamepad). action_attaque Text attack Message when the tool is in the bag, not in hand The text shown when the player strikes a resource without holding the tool they do have in the bag. {outil} is replaced by its name: "Take in hand: Axe". message_en_main Text Prenez en main : {outil} Message when the tool is missing ({outil}: its name) The text shown when the player tries to gather without the tool needed. {outil} is replaced by the tool's name: "You need: {outil}" becomes "You need: Axe". message_outil Text Il faut : {outil}

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Resource given (empty: its name, without number) The name of what the resource puts in the inventory once used up, for example "Wood" for a tree. Empty: the object's name without its number ("Oak 12" gives "Oak"). ressource Text (empty) Quantity given How many of the resource the player receives when it is used up. 0: nothing goes to the inventory. quantite Number 1 from 0 to 1 000 000, as a whole number Hits before it is used up The number of uses before the resource is used up: 1 gathers it in one hit, 5 takes five axe blows. The prompt shows the progress ("Chop 2/5"). coups Number 1 from 1 to 1000, as a whole number Grows back after (seconds, 0: never) The time, in seconds, before the resource comes back after being used up, ready to be gathered again. 0: it never comes back; 60: a minute later. repousse Number 0 from 0 to 86 400 Tool needed, held in hand (empty: none) The name of an item the player must hold in hand to gather, for example "Axe", written exactly as in the inventory: they then strike with the attack. Empty: bare hands, with the interaction (E). outil Text (empty) Prompt text (Chop, Mine, Pick… empty: Interaction's) The word of the prompt in front of the resource, for example "Chop" for a tree or "Mine" for a rock. Empty: the usual text of the Interaction system. verbe Text (empty) Its end, when used up What happens to the resource when it is used up: it vanishes at once, falls, collapses, shrinks or bursts. From the last hit on, it no longer blocks the player. fin Choice in a list Vanishes at once disparait: Vanishes at oncetombe: Falls, away from the playerseffondre: Collapses where it standsretrecit: Shrinkseclate: Bursts Length of its end (s) How many seconds the chosen end lasts: 1 to 2 seconds for a falling tree. No effect if it vanishes at once. duree_fin Number 1.2 from 0.1 to 10 Its own end animation, if its model has one (replaces the chosen end) An animation of the resource's own model, if its file contains one (a tree falling down, for example). It plays instead of the chosen end. animation_ressource Animation of the object's model (empty) Shakes at each hit The resource shakes a little at each hit that does not use it up yet, to show the hit landed. secousse Yes or no yes Player animation (optional) An animation of the player's character, played at each hit: they turn to the resource and play it in place, and holding the key chains the hits. Empty, or missing from their model: the hit is instant. animation Player animation (empty) Moment of the hit in the animation (%) At what moment of the player's animation the hit counts, as a percentage of its length: 50 in the middle, 70 a bit later, when the axe meets the trunk. moment Number 50 from 0 to 100 Animation speed Speeds up or slows down the player's animation: 1 at its original speed, 2 twice as fast (hits closer together), 0.5 twice as slow. vitesse_animation Number 1 from 0.1 to 5

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description collecte.coup cible (id), coups (number), restants (number) The player hit a resource (a use of something carrying collecte). restants is how many hits are left before it is used up. collecte.recolte cible (id), ressource (text), quantite (number), joueur (id?) A resource was used up and gave what it holds. The inventory, if present, has been asked to add it. collecte.epuise cible (id) A resource is used up and is about to disappear (destroyed, or hidden until it grows back): it still exists while this is sent. collecte.repousse cible (id) A used-up resource grew back and can be gathered again. collecte.outil_manquant cible (id), outil (text), joueur (id?) The player tried to gather a resource without the tool it needs: not held in hand (the default, with attack), or not in the inventory (gathering set to the interaction). inventaire.ajouter objet (text), quantite (number), joueur (id?) Ask the inventory to add items, such as a reward. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.plein. With several players, joueur says whose bag; without it, the player whose action is being handled, or every player. action.prise action (text), prise (boolean), par (text), joueur (id?) A system takes a control action for itself, or gives it back (prise false) (version 24): gathering takes attack while the player aims at a resource that needs a tool, so the press chops instead of swinging a weapon. par names who says it ("collecte"). Fighting modules do not strike with that action while any system holds it.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description interaction.utiliser cible (id), joueur (id) The player used the object in reach: a door, a merchant, an item to pick up. Whoever owns that object decides what it does. inventaire.change objet (text), quantite (number), total (number), chargement (boolean?) The quantity of an item changed. total is the new quantity. chargement is true when a saved game gives the items back (game.load): nothing was picked up. inventaire.en_main objet (text), avant (text), place (number), chargement (boolean?), joueur (id?) What the player holds in hand changed (version 24): the slot chosen in the inventory's bar (keys 1 to 9, wheel), an item used up, a load (chargement true). objet is the kind held, "" for empty hands; avant the one held before; place the bar slot (0: nothing). Gathering checks the tool held; a game script equips a sword with it. joueur.occupe occupe (boolean), par (text) The player's hands are taken by something else than fighting (version 23): a building mode where the click places a piece, a tool being aimed. occupe true when it starts, false when it ends; par names who says it ("construction"), so several can overlap. Fighting modules do not strike nor block while any of them keeps the player busy. joueur.depart joueur (id), numero (number) Sent by the engine on the host when a guest leaves the game (they quit, or their connection was lost): their character is removed right after. A module forgets what it kept for them.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • collecte.don: function(default, id) -> resource name (text), quantity (number): what this resource gives when it is used up. The default is its ressource and quantite settings.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Gathering (collecte)
items.text:
Makes what the user calls a resource gatherable: a tree to chop, a rock to mine, a bush to pick, any model. Activating it activates the interaction module; placing it on an object places interaction there too.

  • A resource: an object carrying this system (systems_attach), every child of a group carrying it, or every plant of a plant kind object carrying it (a whole forest at once, see the terrain rules). Set per object or group (systems_set): ressource (what it gives, in the user's language; empty: its name without a trailing number), quantite, coups (uses before it is used up), repousse (seconds before it grows back; 0: never), outil (an item the player must hold in hand, such as "Axe"; empty: bare hands), verbe (the prompt word: Chop, Mine, Pick).
  • A resource with an outil is struck with the attack (left click, X on a gamepad), the tool held in hand: the inventory's bar (keys 1 to 9, the wheel) chooses what is held, announced by inventaire.en_main. This is the user's decision for every game (ADR-029, 11 November 2026). The player aims like the game is seen: the centre of the screen with a character, else what is in front of them, within the interaction reach measured at the trunk or the foot. With the tool only in the bag the message says to take it in hand (message_en_main); without it, message_outil; no hit either way. While the player aims at such a resource, gathering takes the attack (action.prise): combat.basique does not swing too. Holding the attack chains the hits. The game setting recolte_outil = interaction brings back the old way (E, the tool in the bag); do not change it unless the user asks.
  • A resource without outil (berries, a bush) is gathered with the interaction (E by default): each use is one hit. At the last one, what it gives goes to the inventory (inventaire.ajouter: activate inventaire too, or listen to collecte.recolte yourself), and the resource disappears: destroyed, or hidden until it grows back.
  • The prompt shows the key, the verb, the tool to hold in brackets, and the hits so far ("Click: Chop 2/3").
  • animation: a clip of the player's model, read with animation_clips (names differ from one model to another: never guess). The player then turns to the resource and plays it in place; the hit counts at moment (% of the clip, 50 by default), and the gesture lasts the clip's length divided by vitesse_animation. Holding the key chains the hits. Without it, or if the player lacks the clip, each use is an instant hit.
  • Its end, when used up (fin): disparait (vanishes at once, the default), tombe (falls away from the player), seffondre, retrecit, eclate, over duree_fin seconds; it stops blocking at once. If the resource's own model has an end animation, set animation_ressource to it (read its clips with animation_clips on its own file): it replaces the end. secousse (on by default) shakes it at each hit. Its sounds belong to the resource, not to the end: the sons module's recolte_coup and recolte_fin on the resource or its plant kind.
  • React with game.on: collecte.coup (cible, coups, restants) for a hit sound or wood chips, collecte.recolte (cible, ressource, quantite), collecte.epuise (cible, sent before it disappears: read its position to drop logs there), collecte.repousse (cible), collecte.outil_manquant (cible, outil).
  • Give the tool with game.emit("inventaire.ajouter", {objet = "Axe", quantite = 1}), or make an axe an item to pick up with inventaire: it goes into the bar, and into the hand if its slot is the chosen one (game.emit("inventaire.tenir", {objet = "Axe"}) puts it in hand). Its model shows in the hand by itself (see inventaire). Never write your own hotbar, held item or attack-to-gather script: these systems do it.
  • Do not put inventaire on a resource: it would be picked up whole at the first use.
  • Change what a resource gives from your script with game.override("collecte.don", function(default, id) ... end): it returns the resource name and the quantity.
  • Saved games: game.save keeps the hits already struck and the time left before each regrowth (the engine keeps the resource hidden or destroyed); game.load gives them back. Nothing to write.
  • In a large world, resources stay loaded (they carry a system) and asleep when far; one gathered far away still grows back on time.
  • A survival game: collecte gives the materials, fabrication turns them into tools and food, construction spends them on a shelter, besoins makes food matter, jour_nuit gives days and nights. The resource names must match the recipes' and pieces' items exactly.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One for the whole game: resources are shared (a tree cut down is cut for everyone, its regrowth too), but each player has their own gesture, tools, message, and what they harvest goes into their own bag (inventaire.ajouter with joueur).

items.title: Basic combat
items.text:
The player strikes ahead with a key, with the damage, reach and cooldown set on them. It hits what carries Health. For enemies that attack, add "Enemies".

Identifier combat.basique Version 11 Placed on objects yes Also activates Health

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Game tab, Systems section, by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Player action The game's control action that makes the player strike ("attack": the left mouse button by default). action Text attack Several players: players can hurt each other In a game with several players: ticked, a hit also lands on the other players. Unticked (the default), friends do not hurt each other. No effect with a single player. blesser_joueurs Yes or no no A flash and sparks when a hit lands Each hit that lands makes a brief flash, a few sparks and a little dust on the target. Untick it for a game without particles. impact Yes or no yes Action to block The control action to hold to block ("block": the right mouse button by default, LB on a gamepad). It only matters if the player can block. action_parade Text block

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Damage of a hit The health points a hit takes from the target, before its armor. With 25 against an enemy with 100 health points, it takes four hits. degats Number 25 from 0 to 1 000 000 Reach (m) How far, in meters, the hit reaches a target in front of the player: 2 m for a sword, more for a spear. It strikes the nearest one. portee Number 2 from 0.2 to 50 Strike angle ahead (°) The width of the area hit in front of the player, in degrees: 100 covers the front, 360 also hits behind them. Smaller, aiming must be more precise. angle Number 100 from 10 to 360 Time between two hits (s) The minimum time, in seconds, between two hits: 0.5 allows two hits per second at most. With an animation, the next hit also waits for the end of the gesture. recharge Number 0.5 from 0 to 30 Knockback of the target How hard the target hit is pushed back. 0: it does not move. Only characters are knocked back, not still objects. recul Number 4 from 0 to 100 Hit animation (optional) An animation of the player's character, played at each hit; the hit lands at its moment of impact. Empty, or missing from their model: the hit lands at once. animation Player animation (empty) Moment of the hit in the animation (%) At what moment of the animation the hit lands, as a percentage of its length: 50 in the middle, later for a big wind-up swing. moment Number 50 from 0 to 100 Animation speed Speeds up or slows down the hit animation: 1 at its original speed, 2 twice as fast. The next hit waits for the end of the gesture: faster, the player strikes more often. vitesse_animation Number 1 from 0.1 to 5 Share of a hit stopped when blocking (%, 0: cannot block) The share of damage stopped when the player blocks a hit from the front, as a percentage: 70 lets 30 % through, 100 stops everything. 0: the player cannot block. parade Number 0 from 0 to 100 Protected angle ahead (°) The width of the area protected in front of the player while blocking, in degrees: 120 covers the front, 360 also protects the back. angle_parade Number 120 from 10 to 360 Walking speed while blocking (1: normal) The player's walking speed while blocking, compared with normal: 0.5 half, 1 just as fast, 0 standing still. They cannot strike meanwhile. vitesse_parade Number 0.5 from 0 to 1 Block animation (optional) An animation of the player's character, replayed while they block. Empty: they block without changing pose. animation_parade Player animation (empty)

items.title: Controls added to the game
items.text:
They appear in the Game tab, Controls section, where you can change their key.

Control Name for scripts Key Gamepad Block block Right-click LB

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description combat.attaque source (id) Someone struck, whether it hit or not: the stamina module counts it. combat.coup cible (id), source (id), montant (number) An attack hit something. The health module, if present, has been asked to remove the damage. sante.blesser cible (id), montant (number), source (id?) Ask the health module to remove health from an object. sante.garde cible (id), part (number), angle (number) An object protects itself, or stops (part 0): hits coming from in front of it, within angle degrees, lose part of their damage (0 to 1) before its armor. A hit without a source cannot be blocked.

Fighting modules do not strike nor block while any of them keeps the player busy. action.prise action (text), prise (boolean), par (text), joueur (id?) A system takes a control action for itself, or gives it back (prise false) (version 24): gathering takes attack while the player aims at a resource that needs a tool, so the press chops instead of swinging a weapon. par names who says it ("collecte"). Fighting modules do not strike with that action while any system holds it.

items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • combat.degats: function(default, joueur, cible, degats) -> the raw damage of the player's hit on this target. The default returns degats, the value set on the player. For a weapon bonus, a critical hit, a combo.

items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Basic combat (combat.basique)
items.text:
The player strikes the nearest object carrying Health in front of them with a key (attack, the left mouse button by default). Activating it activates the health module.

  • Place it on the player with systems_attach: the player's damage, reach, strike angle, cooldown, knockback and hit animation are their values (systems_set). Without it on the player, the key does nothing. The animation is a clip of the player's model, read with animation_clips (never guess names): the hit lands at moment (% of the clip, 50 by default), and the next strike waits for the end of the gesture, whose length is the clip's divided by vitesse_animation. Without an animation, the hit is instant.
  • What can be hit: objects carrying sante. The damage sent is raw: the target's armor is applied by the health module.
  • It handles the player's hits only. Enemies that move and attack are the module ennemis: add it only if the user asked for enemies that fight.
  • Blocking: set parade on the player (the share of a hit stopped, in %, such as 70 or 100; 0 by default: no blocking). While the action block is held (right mouse button by default, LB on a gamepad), hits from in front within angle_parade lose that share before armor, the player walks at vitesse_parade and cannot strike. animation_parade is a clip of the player's model, replayed while blocking. A blocked hit is announced by sante.pare (cible, source, montant stopped).
  • With the stamina module (endurance), each strike costs stamina, and an exhausted player cannot strike or block.
  • While the game shows the cursor (game.show_cursor(true): an inventory, a menu), or while something keeps the player busy (the event joueur.occupe: construction's building mode, where the click places a piece), the player neither strikes nor blocks. A script of yours that takes the player's hands (aiming a fishing rod) sends joueur.occupe with occupe true, then false, and its own par.
  • While another system takes the attack action for itself (the event action.prise: collecte while the player aims at a resource that needs a tool, so the click chops), the player does not strike with it: one press, one gesture.
  • React to hits: listen to combat.coup (cible, source, montant), for a sound or an effect. Deaths come from the health module: sante.mort.
  • Knockback moves characters only. A dead object stays unless its health values say to remove it.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One copy per player: each player has their own cooldown, block and hits. Players do not hurt each other unless the game setting blesser_joueurs ("Players can hurt each other") is ticked.

items.title: Building
items.text:
The player places pieces in the world: walls, floors, a campfire, any model. In building mode (B), a preview goes where they aim, on a grid or freely: with the view (the centre of the screen) when they play a character, with the cursor from above. A click places the piece and takes its cost from the inventory. A placed piece can be torn down, and gives back part of its cost.

Identifier construction Version 3 Placed on objects no Also activates Inventory

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description construction.pose cible (id), piece (text) The player placed a piece (a copy of its model, cible), and its cost left the inventory. piece is its name (original language). construction.detruit cible (id), piece (text) A placed piece is gone: torn down by the player, by construction.detruire, or killed (sante.mort). Its place on the grid is free again. construction.mode actif (boolean) The building mode opened (actif true: the cursor shows and a preview follows it) or closed. construction.manque piece (text), manque (text) The player tried to place a piece without its cost: manque lists what is missing, in the player's language. joueur.occupe occupe (boolean), par (text) The player's hands are taken by something else than fighting (version 23): a building mode where the click places a piece, a tool being aimed. occupe true when it starts, false when it ends; par names who says it ("construction"), so several can overlap. Fighting modules do not strike nor block while any of them keeps the player busy. inventaire.ajouter objet (text), quantite (number), joueur (id?) Ask the inventory to add items, such as a reward. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.plein. With several players, joueur says whose bag; without it, the player whose action is being handled, or every player. inventaire.retirer objet (text), quantite (number) Ask the inventory to remove items, such as a payment. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.manque if there are not enough.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description construction.detruire cible (id), rendre (boolean?) Ask the building system to remove a placed piece (a storm, an enemy, a script). rendre true gives back part of its cost, as tearing it down would. inventaire.change objet (text), quantite (number), total (number), chargement (boolean?) The quantity of an item changed. total is the new quantity. chargement is true when a saved game gives the items back (game.load): nothing was picked up. inventaire.manque objet (text), quantite (number) Items could not be removed: there are not enough. sante.mort cible (id), source (id?) An object's health reached zero. What happens next belongs to the game: the health module does nothing else, unless its setting says to destroy the object. langue.change langue (text) Sent by the engine when the player changes the game's language (game.set_language, the Menu options). A module redraws what it already shows: its texts go through game.t and game.language.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • construction.permise: function(default, piece, position) -> true, or false and the reason shown (text): whether this piece can be placed there. piece is its name (original language), position a vector. The default is true. To forbid building in a town, near water, or before a quest.

items.title: Building (construction)
items.text:
The player places pieces in the world (walls, floors, a fence, a campfire: any model of the library), pays them from the inventory, and can tear them down. Add it once with modules_add (with inventaire). Use it whenever the user talks about building a shelter, a base, a camp: never write a building script.

Its game setting pieces (modules_set) is a list of rows, in order. A piece row is a piece; the cout rows under it are its cost.

  • piece: nom (shown, in the user's language; it names the piece in events), modele (the id of an object of the scene copied at each placement: create it once, standing on the ground where nothing walks, with visible: false, a collider if it should stop the player, and the systems each copy should have), decalage (on a grid, metres pushed forward along its facing: half a cell for a wall that edges the cell).
  • cout: objet (an inventory kind, as collecte gives it), nombre. A piece without cost is free.
  • Example: [{"sorte": "piece", "nom": "Mur en bois", "modele": "mur_modele", "decalage": 1}, {"sorte": "cout", "objet": "Bois", "nombre": 4}, {"sorte": "piece", "nom": "Feu de camp", "modele": "feu_modele"}, {"sorte": "cout", "objet": "Pierre", "nombre": 3}].
  • Never guess a model's size: measure it (the model's bounds in scene_get, or game.bounds in a script) to choose grille and decalage. The module itself puts each piece's foot on the surface aimed at, from the model's own bounds.
  • A piece that does something: its model's systems go to every copy. A campfire model carrying fabrication (nom_etabli « Feu de camp ») and particules becomes a workbench with flames; a bed model carrying besoins (source_besoin « Fatigue », source_heures 8) lets the player sleep.
  • Playing: the control build (B, or RB on a gamepad) opens the building mode: a preview of the piece goes where the player aims (it blinks where it cannot go, beyond portee too). build_place (click, or X) places it and takes its cost; build_rotate (wheel, or right stick pressed) turns it by rotation degrees; build_next (Q, or ←) or the keys 1 to 9 choose the piece; build_remove (X key, or B) tears down the piece aimed at and gives back rendu % of its cost. build again leaves the mode. A line at the bottom tells the piece, its cost and the keys (aide). While the mode is open the module sends joueur.occupe (occupe true, par « construction »), so combat.basique neither strikes nor blocks: the click places.
  • Aiming (game setting visee): auto (default) follows the game's camera (game.camera_view()): a character in first or third person aims with the view, the centre of the screen, and the camera keeps turning with the mouse, like the building mode of every survival game; a top-down view (the player camera's lowest tilt is 45° or more) or a placed camera aims with the cursor, which shows during the mode. centre or curseur force one. With a gamepad, the view aims (from above: the ground just in front of the player). Leave auto unless the user asks.
  • Game settings: grille (cell size in metres; 0: free placement exactly where the player aims), visee, rotation, portee (metres from the player), rendu, demolir (the player may tear down), aide.
  • Events announced: construction.pose (cible: the new piece, piece: its name), construction.detruit (cible, piece), construction.mode (actif), construction.manque (piece, manque). Send construction.detruire (cible, rendre?) to remove a piece (a storm, an enemy). Placed pieces carry the tag « construction.piece »; the preview carries « construction.apercu ».
  • Forbid building somewhere from your own script, never the module's: game.override("construction.permise", function(default, piece, position) if game.distance(position, game.find("Village")) < 30 then return false, game.t("Pas dans le village.") end return default(piece, position) end).
  • Saved games: game.save keeps the pieces (the engine keeps the copies, the module which piece each one is); game.load gives them back. In a large world, placed pieces stay loaded and asleep when far, like everything a system follows.
  • HUD keys start with construction..
  • Testing: in game_run, give the cost with inventaire.ajouter in a test script, press build, then aim: with the view (third person), turn the camera with pitch/yaw until the centre of the screen is on the ground in front of the player (the default tilt already looks about 4 m ahead); with the cursor (top-down, visee « curseur »), use mouse ([x, y] of the screen). Press build_place; read construction.pose in the report's events, then build_remove on the same spot.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One copy per player: each player has their own build mode, piece, preview and cost (their own inventory), aiming with their own camera (and cursor, from above). What is built is shared: every player sees it (the pieces are shared copies), and the host's saved game keeps it.

items.title: Decal
items.text:
An image projected on what lies under the object: a footprint, an impact, a stain, a puddle, a scorch mark, a sign painted on a wall. Create > Decal places an invisible box that carries it: the image covers its width and depth, and lies on the ground or the wall around its base.

Identifier decalcomanie Version 1 Placed on objects yes Run by the engine yes: the engine runs it itself, without a script

items.title: Decal (decalcomanie)
items.text:
An object carrying this system projects an image on what lies around its base: the ground, a wall, a floor of cubes. A footprint, an impact, a stain, a puddle, a scorch mark, a sign. The system has no script: the renderer projects it. The game report counts decals under decals.

  • Make a decal: create a box (builtin:cube) with visible: false and no collider, then systems_attach this system on it. The image covers the box's width (x) and depth (z), and lies on the surface around the box's base, within half its height above and below (y). Scale the box to size the image: 1 × 0.5 × 1 for a puddle of one metre, 0.3 × 0.3 × 0.5 for a footprint. Turn the box around its height to turn the image.
  • On a wall: tip the box so that its height points out of the wall (rotate 90 degrees around x or z), and place its base on the wall.
  • Per object (systems_set): image (tache, impact, brulure, flaque, pas, trace, or fichier with fichier: an image of the project, from assets_search kind "image"; its transparency is kept), opacite (0 to 1), couleur ("#rrggbb", a tint: dark red for blood, green for poison; white leaves the image as it is).
  • A decal shows as long as its object is in the game: game.destroy removes it. Do not make its box visible: that would show the box.
  • From a script, during the game: game.decal("impact", pos, {size = 0.6, normal = vec(0, 1, 0)}) (a crater where a fireball lands, footprints that follow the player). The game keeps a limited number of them (fewer on a small graphics card): the oldest fades out to make room. See the script reference.
  • It projects on everything inside its box, characters walking through included: keep the box thin over a ground where characters walk.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
The engine runs it once for the whole game: decals are seen by the host.

items.title: Trigger
items.text:
"When… then…" rules without writing code: when the player enters a zone, uses a lever, when a boss dies… then a door opens, a chest appears, the game is won. With ready-made actions, and those written for this game.

Identifier declencheur Version 10 Placed on objects yes
