items.title: Trigger (declencheur)
items.text:
"When… then…" rules placed on objects, so the user gets a game reaction without code: when the player enters a zone, uses a lever, when a boss dies, at the start, after a time, or when an event happens… then show, hide or destroy an object, make a copy appear, teleport the player, go to a scene, end the game, play a sound, play a full-screen video, muffle or mute the sound, show a message, push a moving object, send an event — or run a reusable action written for this game.

  • Place it on the object the rule is about (systems_attach), with its rules in regles: a list, one object per rule. Prefer it to a script for these reactions: the user sees and changes the rules in the object's properties.
  • Each rule: quand (entree, sortie: the object carries zone; utilise: it carries interaction; mort: it carries sante; debut; delai with secondes; evenement with evenement, an event name), fois (une or chaque), attente (seconds before acting), action, and the fields of that action:
  • cible (an object id; empty: the object carrying the rule) for montrer, cacher, basculer, detruire, copier, teleporter (the player goes to it), solide, traversable (on a zone: switches it on or off), son, pousser.
  • copier: lieu (an object where the copy appears; empty: where the copied object is). Usually the copied object is a hidden template.
  • animation: frise (an animation's id, made with timeline_set) and fin (optional: an event sent when it ends, for another rule). cinematique: cinematique (a cutscene's id) and fin. arreter_animation: frise.
  • scene: scene and arrivee. finir: resultat (won or lost) and texte. message: texte, duree. son: son (a sound file, from assets_search kind "sound"). assourdir: groupe (a sound mixer group, or master for all the sound), assourdi (0 clear again, 1 under water), fondu (seconds). couper_son: groupe, coupe (true mutes, false brings it back). video: video (an MP4 file, from assets_search kind "video"), passer (true: the player can skip it), fin (an event sent when it ends or is skipped, to chain the next rule; a video file that cannot be read still sends it), groupe_video (the mixer group of its sound, voice by default: the music lowers under it). pousser: force, hauteur. envoyer: nom (sends that event with cible, source and qui). remplir_besoin: besoin (a need's name, as in the besoins list: « Fatigue ») and montant: the player who triggered the rule gets it back (resting by a fire, a meal at an inn); a need switched off does not change.
  • cible also for ouvrir, fermer (a hinge or slider of the articulation system: a door, a drawbridge, an elevator; its motor drives it to its open or closed stop), casser (its joint gives way and it falls), chiffon (a character falls limp as a ragdoll) and relever (it gets back up).
  • effet: effet (objet: lights again the effect the target carries with the particules system; or a ready-made effect played once on the target: eclats, eclats_bois, eclats_pierre, poussiere, feu, fumee, explosion, etincelles, impact, magie, pluie, neige) and taille_effet (its size, 1 by default). arreter_effet: puts out the effect the target carries (a campfire), and the looping effects scripts put on it.
  • quand casse: the object's joint broke (it carries articulation): a bridge gives way, then a message.
  • cible (a placed light, created with a light field) for allumer (switch on), eteindre (switch off), basculer_lumiere (on or off in turn) and couleur_lumiere, with couleur ("#rrggbb"): a lamp lit by a lever, an alarm turning red.
  • Example, a pressure plate that opens a door: a zone box named Plaque, and on it {"regles": [{"quand": "entree", "action": "cacher", "cible": "<door id>"}]}.
  • Under water: a zone box over the water with {"regles": [{"quand": "entree", "fois": "chaque", "action": "assourdir", "groupe": "master", "assourdi": 1}, {"quand": "sortie", "fois": "chaque", "action": "assourdir", "groupe": "master", "assourdi": 0}]}.
  • A brazier lit by a lever: the particules system on the brazier with boucle true, and on the lever {"quand": "utilise", "fois": "chaque", "action": "effet", "effet": "objet", "cible": "<brazier id>"}; another rule with arreter_effet puts it out. A barrel that explodes when hit: {"quand": "mort", "action": "effet", "effet": "explosion", "taille_effet": 2} then a rule that destroys it.
  • A lever: interaction on the lever and a rule {"quand": "utilise", "fois": "chaque", "action": "basculer", "cible": "<door id>"}.
  • A lamp switched by a lever: {"quand": "utilise", "fois": "chaque", "action": "basculer_lumiere", "cible": "<light id>"}.
  • A drawbridge that lowers when the lever is used, then a chest appears: {"quand": "utilise", "action": "animation", "frise": "pont_baisse", "fin": "pont_en_bas"} on the lever, and {"quand": "evenement", "evenement": "pont_en_bas", "action": "montrer", "cible": "<chest id>"}. A door that moves (slides, swings) is an animation, not a reusable action.

Reusable actions: when the user wants an effect no ready-made action does and that is not a set movement (a set movement such as a door that slides, a bridge that rises or a light that blinks is an animation: timeline_set, then the action animation), write it ONCE as a reusable action, never as a one-off script tied to one object: - A game script named action.<id> (scripts_set; id: lowercase letters, digits, _), which starts with its description in JSON between --[[action and ]]: label and description in fr and en, and fields (settings like a module's: key, type number/text/boolean/choice/object/sound/video/scene, default, label in fr and en, min/max, options; a number takes decimals unless it has "integer": true, for a count). - Its code listens to action.<id>: game.on("action.porte_glissante", function(e) ... end). e.cible is the rule's target (or the object carrying the rule), e.source the object carrying the rule, e.qui who triggered it, and each of its fields by key. - It then appears in the "Then" list of every Trigger, with its fields, next to the ready-made actions; a rule uses it with "action": "<id>" and its values in parametres. The user can reuse it on other objects without asking you again: tell them so. - Example: --[[action {"label": {"fr": "Porte qui glisse", "en": "Sliding door"}, "description": {"fr": "La cible glisse sur le côté.", "en": "The target slides aside."}, "fields": [{"key": "distance", "type": "number", "default": 2, "min": 0, "max": 50, "label": {"fr": "Distance (m)", "en": "Distance (m)"}}]} ]], then the code.

items.text:
One for the whole game: "the player" of a rule is the one who triggered it (who entered the zone, who used the object); its message is shown to that player only, and teleporter moves that player. Rules at the start or after a delay concern no one in particular: their message is shown to everyone.

items.title: Dialogue (dialogue)
items.text:
A character who talks when the player uses them: their lines show one by one in a window at the bottom of the screen, with the player's answers as buttons. Activating it activates interaction; placing it on an object places interaction there too. Use it for every talk the user asks for (a merchant, a guard, a quest giver) rather than a script.

Place it on the character with systems_attach, then fill lignes with systems_set: a list of rows, in order, read like a flowchart. Each row has a sorte:

  • replique: the character says texte. The choix rows right under it are its answers.
  • choix: an answer the player can click (texte is its button). As many as needed. condition hides it unless it is met: objet / sans_objet (condition_objet, condition_quantite), marque / sans_marque (condition_marque), visites (condition_visites: talks with this character already finished).
  • test: a question to the game, which chooses where to go.
  • Yes or no: test: "objet" (test_objet, test_quantite) or test: "marque" (test_marque), with si_oui and si_non.
  • By a number: test: "visites" (talks already finished) or test: "quantite" (how many test_objet the player carries), followed by sortie rows.
  • sortie: an exit of the number test above it: a_partir_de (from this number on, up to the next exit's; the last one counts for "and more") and suite.

How it flows:

  • The dialogue starts at the first row. Tests are crossed until a line to show.
  • suite, si_oui, si_non say where to go next: a row's etiquette (replique and test rows have one), fin to close, or empty for the row after the group.
  • An empty suite goes on to the row after only if that row has no etiquette: a labelled row starts another branch, so the talk ends before it. Give a label to every row a branch leads to, and none to the rows that simply follow.
  • marque (on a line or an answer) sets a word the game remembers, for every dialogue's tests and answers. annonce sends an event at the same moment, for a declencheur rule or a script.

A guard who loses patience, then lets in who has the key:

  1. test objet Clé, si_oui: "entre", si_non empty (the next row)
  2. test visites
  3. its exits: sortie 0 → cle, 1 → encore, 2 → rien, 3 → assez, 4 → cachot
  4. one labelled replique per branch (cle, encore, rien, assez, cachot with annonce: "cachot", entre)

Other details:

  • Answers: a line with no answer shown has a Next button, or End when nothing follows.
  • A merchant: on a character who also carries boutique (opening on use), the dialogue comes first, and its last line (the one with End) also offers "Show me your goods" ("Voir la marchandise"), which closes the conversation and opens the shop (boutique.ouvrir). If a line of the dialogue already sends boutique.ouvrir, that button is not added.
  • Gamepad and keyboard: each new line gives the focus to its first button; A or Enter clicks it, the d-pad or the arrows choose another answer. End is the window's back button (B, Escape); a line with Next or answers has none, so Escape still opens the pause there.
  • Saved games: game.save keeps the marks and the conversations already had with each character, and game.load gives them back.
  • Inventory: objet tests and conditions read the inventaire system (the kind of item, as it stores it), so add it to the game.
  • Marks from scripts: a script sets one with game.emit("dialogue.marquer", {marque = "..."}) (retirer = true removes it) and hears them with dialogue.marque.
  • Language: write every line in the user's language, and keep each line short (two or three sentences). For a game offered in other languages, the lines, answers and name go through the game's translation tables (translations_set): never write a dialogue per language.
  • Name and prompt: the name at the top is nom (empty: the object's name). Set the interaction prompt texte to "Talk" in the user's language.
  • Events: dialogue.choix (cible, choix, texte, etiquette), dialogue.debut and dialogue.fin (cible). game.emit("dialogue.ouvrir", {cible = id}) starts a character's dialogue from a zone or a script.
  • Game settings: pause (the world stops during a dialogue, on by default), and bas and largeur, as shares of the screen (where the window ends at the bottom and how wide it is; it grows upwards).
  • The map: the user sees the dialogue as a map in the editor (the character's properties, "Show the map"). It is a flowchart from Start to an End per branch, with boxes for lines, diamonds for tests, and named arrows (an answer, yes, no, "4 and more"). Labels that lead nowhere show in red there: check yours. The user can also edit the dialogue in that map (reconnect an arrow by dragging it, add or remove steps): read lignes again before changing a dialogue they may have touched.
  • Testing: in game_run, walk to the character, press interact, then click the buttons. The report's hud gives each button's area (dialogue.suivant, dialogue.choix.1...).

items.title: Stamina (endurance)
items.text:
Place it on the player (systems_attach): running, jumping and striking (with combat.basique) cost stamina; resting gives it back after a short delay. At zero, the player is exhausted: they can still walk, but not run, jump or strike until they regain a share of it (reprise). Placed on anything else, it does nothing.

  • The player's values (systems_set): maximum, costs, recovery, delay, share to regain.
  • For the whole game (modules_set): the bar under the health bar (HUD keys endurance and endurance.fond), dimmed while exhausted, its place, size and color.
  • Know the value: listen to endurance.change (valeur, max, epuise), announced on the first step, then when it changes.
  • Only running, jumping and the strikes of combat.basique cost stamina. If the user wants another action to tire the player, say it is not available yet.
  • It uses game.set_player_can_run and game.set_player_can_jump: do not call them yourself while this module is in the game.

items.title: Enemies
items.text:
What carries this system patrols, chases the player when it sees them, and hits them in reach, with its own values: an early skeleton and a boss have neither the same speed nor the same damage. They walk around walls.

Identifier ennemis Version 6 Placed on objects yes Also activates Health Also needs, on the same object Health

items.title: Settings for the whole game

In the Game tab, Systems section, by opening the system's card.

items.title: Enemies (ennemis)
items.text:
Objects carrying this system become characters with a state machine: they patrol around their spot, chase the player once they see them, hit them in reach, and go back home when they lose them. Placing it on an object places Health there too. Add it only if the user asked for enemies that attack.

  • Place it on each kind of enemy, best on a group: "Early skeletons" with low damage and speed, "Late skeletons" with high values, the boss alone with its own. Set them with systems_set, and the Health values (health, armor) the same way. A child can change one value for itself.
  • Several enemies at once: set the game setting attaquants_max (modules_set), usually 1 or 2. Only that many strike at the same time; the others wait their turn at distance_attente, circling the player, and step in when a place is free. With the default 0, all strike together: five skeletons in reach kill the player in seconds.
  • States: patrouille, poursuite, attaque, attente (waits its turn), retour, mort. Each change is announced by ennemi.etat (cible, etat): listen to it for a growl, an alert icon, a music change.
  • They walk around obstacles (objects with a collider) to reach the player or go back home. A closed room keeps them out. With vue on, they still have to see the player first.
  • With vue on, walls with a collider hide the player; they give up after 3 s without seeing them, or beyond abandon.
  • Their hits go through the health module, like the player's: the player's armor applies. They are announced by combat.coup. When the player dies, they all go back home. A dead enemy stops; it is removed only if its health values say so.
  • Animations: give the clip names of their model (read them with animation_clips); without them, nothing plays.
  • Enemies cloned during the game from one carrying the system join in within half a second, with its values.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One for the whole game: each enemy chases the nearest living player it sees and keeps them while it sees them; when that player falls or is lost, it looks for another, or goes home.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description fabrication.fabrique objet (text), quantite (number), etabli (text) The player crafted a recipe: its ingredients left the inventory and objet (quantite of it) came in. etabli is the workbench where it was made, empty bare-handed. fabrication.manque objet (text), manque (text?), etabli (text?) A recipe could not be crafted: manque lists what is missing, in the player's language ("2 Wood, 1 Stone"), or etabli names the workbench it needs. inventaire.ajouter objet (text), quantite (number), joueur (id?) Ask the inventory to add items, such as a reward. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.plein. With several players, joueur says whose bag; without it, the player whose action is being handled, or every player. inventaire.retirer objet (text), quantite (number) Ask the inventory to remove items, such as a payment. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.manque if there are not enough.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description fabrication.ouvrir etabli (text?) Ask the crafting system to open its window, with the recipes of the workbench named etabli (empty or missing: bare-handed): a Trigger rule, a button of a drawn screen. fabrication.fabriquer objet (text), etabli (text?) Ask the crafting system to craft the recipe that gives objet, as its button would, at the workbench named etabli (empty or missing: bare-handed). Refused, with fabrication.manque, if something is missing. interaction.utiliser cible (id), joueur (id) The player used the object in reach: a door, a merchant, an item to pick up. Whoever owns that object decides what it does. inventaire.change objet (text), quantite (number), total (number), chargement (boolean?) The quantity of an item changed. total is the new quantity. chargement is true when a saved game gives the items back (game.load): nothing was picked up. inventaire.plein objet (text) An item could not be added: every slot holds another kind of item. inventaire.manque objet (text), quantite (number) Items could not be removed: there are not enough. hud.clic cible (text), joueur (id?) A button of the HUD was clicked: pressed, then released on it; or chosen with A (Enter) while it has the gamepad or keyboard focus; or the window's back button (back = true), with B (Escape). cible is the button's key (game.hud_button), joueur the player who clicked (a guest clicks on their own computer; the host plays the click). Announced by the engine, before the scripts' on_update of that step.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • fabrication.permise: function(default, recette) -> true, or false and the reason shown (text): whether this recipe can be crafted now. recette is its title (the product's original name). The default is true. To unlock a recipe with a quest, a book read, a level.
  • fabrication.texte: function(default, key) -> the text the crafting window shows for that key: titre, titre_etabli, aucune, fabriquer, fermer, fabrique, manque, place, il_faut, refus. It may hold {objet}, {n} and {etabli}, replaced afterwards (in the player's language). The default is the game's translation of the text in the original language (translations_get lists them as built-in texts of the crafting window); without one, French or English, after the player's language.

items.title: Crafting (fabrication)
items.text:
Recipes that turn items of the inventory into another item: three wood and two stones make an axe. Add it once with modules_add (with inventaire and interaction). Use it whenever the user talks about crafting, making, cooking, forging or building tools: never write a crafting script.

Its game setting recettes (modules_set) is a list of rows, in order. A recette row starts a recipe; the ingredient rows under it are what it needs.

  • recette: objet (the item it gives, an inventory kind, in the user's language; it also names the recipe), quantite (how many one crafting gives), etabli (the workbench needed, by its name; empty: bare-handed, anywhere).
  • ingredient: ingredient (an inventory kind), nombre, garde (on: the player must have it but keeps it, a tool such as a hammer).
  • Example, an axe by hand and cooked meat at a campfire: [{"sorte": "recette", "objet": "Hache", "quantite": 1}, {"sorte": "ingredient", "ingredient": "Bois", "nombre": 3}, {"sorte": "ingredient", "ingredient": "Pierre", "nombre": 2}, {"sorte": "recette", "objet": "Viande cuite", "etabli": "Feu de camp"}, {"sorte": "ingredient", "ingredient": "Viande crue", "nombre": 1}].
  • A workbench is an object of the world carrying this system (systems_attach; interaction comes with it): using it (E) opens the window with its recipes and the bare-handed ones. Its name is nom_etabli, or its name without a trailing number: a « Feu de camp 3 » is a « Feu de camp ». A piece the player builds with construction keeps its model's systems: a campfire model carrying fabrication becomes a workbench wherever it is built.
  • The window: the control craft (C, or the left stick pressed on a gamepad) opens it with the bare-handed recipes, plus those of a workbench within reach; it closes with the same key or Close (B / Escape). A recipe lacking something shows in grey with what is missing (montrer_impossibles). pause_fenetre stops the world meanwhile.
  • Spell every item exactly as the inventory stores it: the same kind as what collecte gives (ressource) and what the player picks up.
  • Events announced: fabrication.fabrique (objet, quantite, etabli), fabrication.manque (objet, manque or etabli). Send fabrication.ouvrir (etabli?) to open the window from a declencheur rule or a drawn screen's button, fabrication.fabriquer (objet, etabli?) to craft without the window.
  • Reserve a recipe until something happened (a book read, a quest done) from your own script, never the module's: game.override("fabrication.permise", function(default, recette) if recette == "Arc" and not appris then return false, game.t("Il faut d'abord lire le livre du chasseur.") end return default(recette) end). A refused recipe is not shown.
  • Texts follow the player's language; its own texts (Crafting, Craft, Missing...) are built-in texts listed by translations_get. Change one word with game.override("fabrication.texte", ...).
  • Saved games: nothing of its own to keep (the inventory keeps the items).
  • Gamepad and keyboard: the window's buttons get the focus like every window; B or Escape closes it (fabrication.fermer). HUD keys start with fabrication..
  • Testing: in game_run, give the ingredients with inventaire.ajouter in a test script (or gather them), press craft, then send fabrication.fabriquer or click fabrication.faire.1 (the first recipe shown); read fabrication.fabrique and the inventory in the report's hud.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One copy per player: each player has their own window and ingredients (their own inventory); a workbench serves whoever uses it.

items.title: Interaction (interaction)
items.text:
Lets the player use the nearest object carrying this system with a key (interact, E by default), and shows a prompt such as "E : Door". It never decides what using does.

  • Make an object usable: place the system on it with systems_attach, or on a group so that all its children are usable. Its prompt shows texte if set (systems_set, such as "Open" or "Talk"), otherwise the object's name: name it in the user's language.
  • React when it is used: game.on("interaction.utiliser", function(e) if e.cible == door then ... end end). Doors, merchants, levers and talks are scripts of the game that listen to this event.
  • interaction.proche tells which object is in reach, or none (cible missing): use it to highlight something.
  • Items to pick up carry the system inventaire, which places this one with it: do not handle them yourself.
  • For the whole game: the reach, the action, and whether the prompt shows. The prompt uses the HUD key interaction.invite.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One copy per player: each player has their own prompt, and interaction.utiliser carries joueur, the player who used the object.

items.title: Interface (interface)
items.text:
The look of everything the game shows on screen: panels, buttons, text fields, texts. The system has no script: the engine applies it to the HUD. Add it once with modules_add; it is for the whole game, not placed on objects.

  • Its settings (modules_set) are the default look of every HUD element: fond_panneaux (panel background), fond_boutons (button and field background), accent (hovered button, selected field, scroll bar), texte (text color) as #rrggbb colors; taille_texte (text height, a share of the screen height, 0.03 by default); arrondi (corner rounding, a share of the screen height, 0 for square corners); opacite (background opacity, 0 to 1).
  • A value a script gives (color, alpha, size, text_color) wins over the theme. To let the user restyle the whole interface from one place, do not give colors in scripts: use the theme.
  • When the user asks for a style ("dark and gold", "like a parchment", "bigger text"), change these settings instead of every script.
  • Without the system, the HUD keeps its former look (texts slightly bigger than buttons).
  • Build menus with game.hud_panel and parent (see scripts_reference): the engine places the elements, wraps texts, scrolls long lists, and announces hud.clic and hud.valider.
  • Check a menu in game_run: the report's hud gives each element's rect as the engine placed it, hidden for what is outside a scrolled panel's frame, and lines for wrapped texts. Then look at it with capture_steps.

Once full, they no longer pick up a new kind, but still more of the kinds they have. places Number 20 from 1 to 1000, as a whole number Pick up by walking over, without a key Ticked: the player picks up an item just by walking over it. Unticked: they have to use it (E by default). au_contact Yes or no no Reach to pick up by walking over (m) The distance, in meters, at which an item is picked up by walking over it, when picking up by contact is ticked. distance_contact Number 1.2 from 0.1 to 10 One bag for the whole group (several players) In a game with several players: ticked, all players share the same bag; what one picks up, the others can use. Unticked, each has their own. No effect in a single-player game. sac_commun Yes or no no Show the content on screen Shows at the top right of the screen what the player carries, such as "Apple x3". afficher Yes or no yes Inventory window with a key (I) Ticked: the Open the inventory control (I, or Back on a gamepad) opens a window with one slot per kind of item, and closes it. Beyond four rows, the grid scrolls with the mouse wheel. colonnes Number 5 from 1 to 8, as a whole number Stop the game while the window is open Ticked: the world stops while the inventory window is open. Unticked: the game goes on behind it, enemies included. pause_fenetre Yes or no yes A bar of items to hold in hand (keys 1 to 9, wheel) Ticked: as in survival games, a bar of slots chooses what the player holds in hand, with keys 1 to 9, the mouse wheel or the gamepad's d-pad left (it goes round the slots). What they pick up goes into it by itself, and the key of the slot already chosen puts the item away. Untick it if your game draws its own bar (an editor screen, for example): the keys still work. afficher_barre Yes or no yes Place of the bar Where the bar of items in hand is drawn on screen: at the bottom in the middle, as in most games, at the top, or in a column on one side. place_barre Choice in a list At the bottom, in the middle bas: At the bottom, in the middlehaut: At the top, in the middlegauche: On the left, in a columndroite: On the right, in a column Show the item held in the character's hand Ticked: the model of the item held appears in the character's hand and follows their moves. items.text:

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description inventaire.change objet (text), quantite (number), total (number), chargement (boolean?) The quantity of an item changed. total is the new quantity. chargement is true when a saved game gives the items back (game.load): nothing was picked up. inventaire.plein objet (text) An item could not be added: every slot holds another kind of item. inventaire.manque objet (text), quantite (number) Items could not be removed: there are not enough. inventaire.choisi objet (text), total (number) The player clicked a slot of the inventory window: objet is the kind of item, total how many they carry. What it does belongs to the game: eat, equip, read. inventaire.en_main objet (text), avant (text), place (number), chargement (boolean?), joueur (id?) What the player holds in hand changed (version 24): the slot chosen in the inventory's bar (keys 1 to 9, wheel), an item used up, a load (chargement true). objet is the kind held, "" for empty hands; avant the one held before; place the bar slot (0: nothing). Gathering checks the tool held; a game script equips a sword with it.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description interaction.utiliser cible (id), joueur (id) The player used the object in reach: a door, a merchant, an item to pick up. Whoever owns that object decides what it does. inventaire.ajouter objet (text), quantite (number), joueur (id?) Ask the inventory to add items, such as a reward. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.plein. With several players, joueur says whose bag; without it, the player whose action is being handled, or every player. inventaire.retirer objet (text), quantite (number) Ask the inventory to remove items, such as a payment. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.manque if there are not enough. inventaire.tenir objet (text?), place (number?), joueur (id?) Ask the inventory to hold something in hand (version 24): a bar slot (place), or a kind of item (objet; one outside the bar takes the chosen slot). objet "" puts the item away: empty hands. joueur.occupe occupe (boolean), par (text) The player's hands are taken by something else than fighting (version 23): a building mode where the click places a piece, a tool being aimed. occupe true when it starts, false when it ends; par names who says it ("construction"), so several can overlap. Fighting modules do not strike nor block while any of them keeps the player busy. hud.clic cible (text), joueur (id?) A button of the HUD was clicked: pressed, then released on it; or chosen with A (Enter) while it has the gamepad or keyboard focus; or the window's back button (back = true), with B (Escape). cible is the button's key (game.hud_button), joueur the player who clicked (a guest clicks on their own computer; the host plays the click). Announced by the engine, before the scripts' on_update of that step. langue.change langue (text) Sent by the engine when the player changes the game's language (game.set_language, the Menu options). A module redraws what it already shows: its texts go through game.t and game.language.

items.title: Inventory (inventaire)
items.text:
Keeps what the player carries, grouped by kind. Activating it activates the interaction module; placing it on an object places interaction there too, so the player can use it.

  • An item to pick up: an object carrying this system (systems_attach), or every child of a group carrying it. Its kind is nom if set (systems_set), otherwise its name without a trailing number: "Apple 3" is an "Apple". quantite is how many one pickup gives: a bag of 50 coins. Name items in the user's language.
  • Picking up: the player uses the item (E by default), or walks over it if the game setting au_contact is on. The item leaves the world.
  • Give or take items from your scripts, such as a reward or a payment: game.emit("inventaire.ajouter", {objet = "Apple", quantite = 2}), game.emit("inventaire.retirer", {objet = "Gold", quantite = 10}).
  • Know what the player has: listen to inventaire.change (objet, quantite, total). A shop checks total before selling, or listens to inventaire.manque, sent when there are not enough.
  • inventaire.plein is sent when every slot holds another kind of item (game setting places).
  • The content shows at the top right with the HUD key inventaire.
  • The window: the control inventory (I, or Back on a gamepad) opens a grid with one slot per kind, and closes it (game setting fenetre). It scrolls beyond four rows; colonnes sets the slots per row; pause_fenetre stops the world while it is open. Its HUD keys start with inventaire..
  • Gamepad and keyboard: the first slot has the focus, the d-pad or the arrows move it, A or Enter chooses it, B or Escape closes the window (inventaire.fermer is its back button).
  • Saved games: game.save keeps what the player carries, and game.load gives it back; then the inventory announces each kind again with inventaire.change and chargement = true (nothing was picked up), so that every system knows the totals. Do not re-add items after a load.
  • The item in hand (game setting barre, on by default): a bar of cases_barre slots (5) at the bottom of the screen (place_barre; afficher_barre off if the game draws its own). What is picked up fills the first free slot; keys 1 to 9, the wheel (item_next, item_previous) and the d-pad left (item_next: it goes round the slots; every other gamepad button already belongs to a system) choose the slot, and its key again puts the item away. What is held is announced by inventaire.en_main (objet, "" for empty hands, avant, place): collecte gathers with the tool held, a game script equips a sword with it. Choose it from a script with game.emit("inventaire.tenir", {objet = "Axe"}) (or place, or objet = ""). In the window, a number key puts the hovered slot at that place of the bar. The bar, the chosen slot and what is held are saved; each player has their own.
  • Its model in the hand (montrer_en_main, on): a copy of its model follows the character's hand bone, found by measuring the skeleton (game.hand_bone: a bone made for holding under the right hand, else the right hand; os_main overrides it). The model comes from the list en_main (a row per kind: objet, modele, an object of the scene, usually hidden, and an offset and rotation along the bone), else from the first item of that kind picked up. Best: set the model in the character's hand in the editor (entities_create with attach_bone), check it with a capture, hide it, and name it in en_main: its exact place is reused. Do not leave a visible model in the hand, nor write a script that shows or hides one.
  • A click on a slot sends inventaire.choisi (objet, total). What it does belongs to the game: eat an apple (inventaire.retirer, then sante.soigner), equip a sword, read a letter. Write that in a game script, or a declencheur rule on the event.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One copy per player: each player has their own bag by default. The game setting sac_commun ("One bag for the whole group") gives everyone the same bag. The host's saved game keeps each guest's bag under their player key: they find it again when they come back.

items.title: Day and night
items.text:
Time goes by: the sun rises, crosses the sky and sets, then night falls, darker and bluish, and the day comes back. Broad daylight is the scene's light as you set it. The chosen lamps light up at night, and a clock can show.

Identifier jour_nuit Version 1 Placed on objects no

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Game tab, Systems section, by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Length of a whole day (minutes of play) How many minutes of play 24 hours of the world last, night included: 20 gives about 13 minutes of day and 7 of night with the default hours. 1440 follows real time. duree Number 20 from 1 to 1440 Time when the game starts The world's time when the game starts, from 0 to 24: 8 for the morning, 12 for noon, 22 to start at night. heure_depart Number 8 from 0 to 24 Sunrise (hour) The hour the sun appears on the horizon. The light rises during the first hour. lever Number 6 from 0 to 24 Sunset (hour) The hour the sun disappears below the horizon. Night is the time between sunset and sunrise. coucher Number 20 from 0 to 24 Moonlight (share of the sun) The strength of the light in the middle of the night, as a share of the sun's at noon: 0.15 lets one see the way, 0 gives a pitch-black night where only lamps give light. nuit_lumiere Number 0.15 from 0 to 1 Moonlight color The tint of the light at night: a pale blue by default. couleur_nuit Color #8ea6e0 Night sky The color of the sky and the horizon in the middle of the night, toward which the scene's sky darkens at dusk. ciel_nuit Color #0b1020 Rising and setting sun color The warm tint of the sun near the horizon, in the morning and the evening. It blends into the scene's sun color as it rises. couleur_aube Color #ff9a5c Tag of the lamps lit at night (empty: none) The placed lights carrying this tag, such as "lamp", light up at sunset and go out at sunrise: street lamps, torches, windows. lumieres Text (empty) Scenes without the cycle, separated by commas (interiors) The scenes where the light does not change, such as "Cave, Inn": an interior keeps its own. Time still goes by there. scenes_exclues Text (empty) Show the day and the time Shows at the top of the screen the world's day and time, such as "Day 2 — 07:30". horloge Yes or no no

A module redraws what it already shows: its texts go through game.t and game.language.

items.title: Day and night (jour_nuit)
items.text:
Time goes by in the world: the sun rises, crosses the sky and sets, night falls, darker and bluish, then the day comes back. Add it once with modules_add. Use it whenever the user asks for days and nights, a clock, nights that are dangerous: never write a sun script.

  • Broad daylight is the scene's own light (world_set: sun direction, color, intensity, sky): set the scene as it should look at noon, and the module only tilts and darkens it. The sun rises a quarter turn before its noon place and sets a quarter turn after.
  • Game settings (modules_set): duree (minutes of play for 24 hours of the world, 20 by default), heure_depart (0 to 24: match the time of day the user chose; 12 at noon, 7 in the morning, 19 at sunset, 22 at night), lever and coucher (hours), nuit_lumiere (the moon's strength, a share of the sun: 0.15 lets one see, 0 is pitch black), couleur_nuit (moonlight), ciel_nuit (the night sky), couleur_aube (the warm sun at dawn and dusk), lumieres (a tag: the placed lights carrying it light up at sunset and go out at sunrise), scenes_exclues (scene names, separated by commas, where the light stays as set: interiors, caves), horloge (shows « Day 2 — 07:30 » at the top).
  • Events announced: jour_nuit.heure (heure, jour), jour_nuit.lever (jour), jour_nuit.coucher (jour). React with a declencheur rule or a script: wolves come out at night, a shop closes. Send jour_nuit.avancer (heures) to move the clock on (a night in a bed: the besoins system's source does it with source_heures), jour_nuit.aller_a (heure) to skip to a time.
  • A script can read and change the light itself with game.environment() and game.set_environment({...}) (a storm); with this module, change the scene's light with world_set instead, or the module overrides it on the next step.
  • Saved games: game.save keeps the day and the time, and the engine keeps the light; game.load gives them back. Nothing to write.
  • In a large world, time goes by the same everywhere; lights tagged for the night switch even far away.
  • HUD key: jour_nuit.horloge.
  • Testing: check the events in game_run (jour_nuit.coucher after the right number of steps: with duree 20, one hour of the world is 50 seconds of play), or log game.environment().sun_intensity from a test script; capture_steps shows the light at those steps (start the game at the hour to see with heure_depart).

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One for the whole game: the time of day, the sun and the clock are the same for everyone.

items.title: Menu
items.text:
The title screen when the game starts, and the pause with Escape: Resume, Options (in sections: sound, display with the graphics and, for a translated game, the language, controls), Quit. The game stops while the menu is open, and it takes the look of the Interface system. A game with the Multiplayer setting also has Host and Join there.

Identifier menu Version 10 Placed on objects no

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Game tab, Systems section, by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Title screen at start Ticked: the game opens on a screen with its title and a Play button, the world stopped behind it. Unticked: play starts at once. ecran_titre Yes or no yes Title shown (empty: the game's) The big title of the title screen. Empty: the game's title, set in the game settings, Window section. titre Text (empty) Pause with Escape Ticked: the Pause control (Escape, or Start on a gamepad) stops the game and opens the Resume, Options, Quit menu. It closes it too. pause Yes or no yes Options button: volumes, graphics and controls Adds an Options button: the player sets the master volume and that of each sound mixer group there (music, effects, ambience, voice, interface…), chooses the graphics (the quality, Low, Medium or High, particles included; the upscaling and its method, None, FSR (all cards) or DLSS if you provided it; ray tracing, Automatic, On or Off, if their card has it and the game allows it, and its indirect lighting, the light bounced by surfaces in High quality), changes the key of each control and, if the game is translated, chooses their language. The player finds these choices again the next time the game starts; the game's own settings do not change. options Yes or no yes Quit button Adds a Quit button, which closes the game. quitter Yes or no yes Host and Join buttons (multiplayer game) In a game with the Multiplayer setting (game settings): the title screen and the pause have Host a game and Join a game (you type the host's address). The host's pause then says how many guests are there, and lets them stop the online game. Without the Multiplayer setting, these buttons do not show. en_ligne Yes or no yes Darkening of the game behind the menu (0: none, 1: black) How much the stopped game darkens behind the menu: 0 leaves it as it is, 1 hides it completely. voile Number 0.55 from 0 to 1

items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • menu.texte: function(default, key) -> the text the menu shows for that key: jouer, reprendre, options, quitter, pause, retour, son, affichage, master, touches, attente, annuler_touche, langue, graphismes, qualite, qualite_low, qualite_medium, qualite_high, echelle, echelle_off, echelle_native, echelle_quality, echelle_balanced, echelle_performance, echelle_ultra_performance, methode, methode_none, methode_fsr, methode_dlss, oui, non, anticrenelage, anticrenelage_auto, anticrenelage_taa, anticrenelage_smaa, anticrenelage_fxaa, anticrenelage_none, ray_tracing, ray_tracing_auto, ray_tracing_on, ray_tracing_off, ray_tracing_lourd, ray_tracing_coupe, lumiere_indirecte, lumiere_indirecte_aide, heberger, rejoindre, adresse, rejoindre_ok, connexion, en_ligne, hors_ligne, echec, and the id of each sound mixer group (music, effects, ambience, voice, ui...). The default is the game's translation of the text in the original language (translations_get lists them as built-in texts of the menu); without one, French or English, after the player's language; a group's default is its name.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Menu (menu)
items.text:
The title screen when the game starts, and the pause menu with Escape: Resume, Options (the master volume and one volume per group of the sound mixer: music, effects, ambience, voice, ui and the game's own groups; the graphics; a new key for every control), Quit. Add it once with modules_add; it is for the whole game, not placed on objects. Use it whenever the user wants a title screen, a pause or an options menu: do not write one in a script.

  • The world stops while the menu is open (game.pause): the player, enemies, physics, animations and game.time. The menu takes the look of the interface system: change the style there, not here.
  • Game settings (modules_set): ecran_titre (title screen at start), titre (the title shown; empty: the game's title from the game settings, Window), pause (Escape opens the pause menu), options and quitter (show those buttons), voile (how dark the stopped game gets behind the menu, 0 to 1).
  • Texts follow the player's language: the menu's own texts (Play, Options, Graphics...) are built-in texts of the system, listed by translations_get like the game's texts. Translate them there for every language the game offers; without a translation, the menu shows its French or English text. For a translated game (world_set languages), Options shows a Language row: each click moves to the next offered language, and the game remembers it. The titre setting is translated with the game's tables. To change a word, override menu.texte from a game script: game.override("menu.texte", function(default, key) if key == "jouer" then return "Commencer" end return default(key) end).
  • Options are arranged in sections, one tab each (HUD keys menu.onglet.son, menu.onglet.affichage, menu.onglet.touches): Sound (the volumes), Display (the language of a translated game and the graphics; only when there is something to choose) and Controls (the keys). A section taller than half the screen scrolls inside the window, which never overflows, however many sound groups or controls the game has. In game_run, click a tab before the rows of its section: only the open section is in the report's hud.
  • Graphics, in Options (Display section), for a game on screen: Quality (Low, Medium or High: shadows, lights, water, glow, terrain and plant distances, and the particles budget; the machine chooses at first, Low on an integrated chip, High on a graphics card), Upscaling (Off, anti-aliasing only, Quality 67 %, Balanced 58 %, Performance 50 %, Ultra performance 33 %; the game's own window.upscaling at first), Shadows (As quality at first, then High, Medium, Low, Off: for the sun and every light, effects' lights included; Off removes every shadow, the lightest; over the scene's shadowQuality), the upscaling method (None, FSR on every card, and DLSS (NVIDIA) only when the user provided NVIDIA's files and turned DLSS on in the game settings (Game window), on an RTX card; shown only when FSR or DLSS works there); Ray tracing (Automatic, On, Off) only on a graphics card that has it, when the game allows it (« ray_tracing » in world_set window, allowed by default). Automatic draws shadows and reflections with rays only on a dedicated graphics card in Medium and High quality; On forces it, with a short warning under the line where it is heavy (an integrated chip, Low quality); when the graphics card's memory is full, the game turns rays off by itself (classic shadows) and a short line under it says so, until the player picks another value. Under it, Indirect lighting (On at first, or Off; key menu.lumiere_indirecte, with a short line saying what it does): the light bounced by surfaces, ray traced, only in High quality (about 1 to 2 ms). Each click moves to the next value, at once. The menu uses game.graphics and game.set_graphics: a game script can call them too, but never alongside the menu's options. Not shown in game_run without capture: nothing is drawn there.
  • The player's choices in Options (the volume of each sound group, the graphics and the keys and gamepad buttons they changed) are kept from one launch of the game to the next, in the save slot menu-options: the exported game keeps it with the player's saves, the editor with the saves of its test runs. The game settings and the project are never changed by it. Do not use that slot name in a game script; game.delete_save("menu-options") gives the player the game's own volumes, graphics and keys back at the next launch. A control the game no longer has is forgotten. In game_run, saves start empty: every run begins with the game's own volumes, graphics and keys.
  • menu.jouer is sent when the player leaves the title screen: start an intro, a timer or a music on it rather than in on_start, which runs behind the title. A declencheur rule can use it too ("when the event menu.jouer"). menu.pause (ouvert) is sent when the pause menu opens or closes.
  • In game_run, the title screen waits for a click on Play: show nothing else first. The report's hud gives the area of menu.jouer; click its centre with mouse and buttons (a short segment with left, then one without). Turn ecran_titre off only if the user does not want a title screen.
  • Gamepad and keyboard: with a gamepad, Play (or Resume) has the focus at once; the d-pad or the arrows move it, A or Enter clicks, B or Escape goes back from the options and closes the pause (Resume and Back are the window's back buttons). While a key is being changed in the options, the menu turns the engine's navigation off (game.hud_navigation(false)), so that A, B and the arrows can be bound too.
  • HUD keys start with menu.: do not use that prefix in a game script.

items.title: Several players
items.text: One copy per player: in a game hosted online, a menu does not stop the game. A guest has no title screen (they join a game already running) and no options (their sound, display and keys belong to their own computer): only Resume and Quit, and Quit makes them leave the game.

items.title: Host and Join (several players)
items.text:
In a game with the « Multiplayer » setting, the title screen and the pause have « Host a game » and « Join a game » (setting « en_ligne », on by default). Join opens a screen with a field for the host's address and a Join button; a refusal shows there. While hosting, the pause says how many guests are there and has « Stop the online game ». They call game.host, game.join(address) and game.leave_online; only the game on screen does it (in game_run, game.network() says available=false and the buttons do not show). Texts: heberger, rejoindre, adresse, rejoindre_ok, connexion, en_ligne, hors_ligne, echec (hook « menu.texte »).

items.title: Particle effect
items.text:
Particles coming out of the object: a campfire, a torch, smoke, sparks, magic, rain or snow around the player. Choose the effect, its size, its colour and its amount; it loops or plays once. For an effect on its own, Create > Particle effect places an invisible box that carries it.

Identifier particules Version 1 Placed on objects yes Run by the engine yes: the engine runs it itself, without a script

items.text:
In the Game tab, Systems section, by opening the system's card.

None.

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Effect What the object gives off: fire (a campfire; a torch with a size of 0.4), smoke, sparks, magic, rain or snow (placed on the player, they follow them), dust, chips, an explosion. effet Choice in a list Fire (with a little smoke) feu: Fire (with a little smoke)fumee: Smokeetincelles: Sparksmagie: Magicpluie: Rainneige: Snowpoussiere: Dusteclats: Chips (the object's colour)eclats_bois: Wood chipseclats_pierre: Stone chipsexplosion: Explosionimpact: Hit impact Size The size of the whole effect: 1 for a campfire, 0.4 for a torch, 3 for a big blaze. For rain and snow, the width of the area where they fall. taille Number 1 from 0.05 to 20 Colour The effect's colour: its own (a yellow and red fire, grey smoke), or a chosen colour (a blue fire, green magic). teinte Choice in a list The effect's own effet: The effect's ownchoisie: A chosen colour Chosen colourshown only if Colour is “A chosen colour” The particles' starting colour; they darken as they age, like the original effect. couleur Color #4da6ff Amount The number of particles, multiplied: 0.5 for a lighter effect, 2 for a fuller one. A small graphics card keeps fewer at a time. quantite Number 1 from 0 to 10 Looping (unticked: only once, when the game starts) Ticked: the effect runs as long as the object is there (a campfire). For a torch's flame, the height of its tip; for rain, 0 is enough: it falls from high up. hauteur Number 0 from -50 to 50 Effect lightshown only if Effect is “Fire (with a little smoke)”, “Explosion”, “Magic”, “Sparks” or “Hit impact” A fire, an explosion, magic or sparks light up what is around them: a light that follows the effect, flickers with the fire and grows with its size. items.title: Particle effect (particules)
items.text:
An object carrying this system gives off particles, simulated by the game and drawn by the renderer: a campfire, a torch, smoke, sparks, magic, rain or snow. The system has no script: the engine runs it. The same game gives the same particles, and the game report counts them under particles.

  • Place it on the object the effect comes from (systems_attach): a campfire model, a torch, a cauldron. For an effect on its own (a fire in the middle of a camp, snow over a valley), create a box (builtin:cube) with visible: false, no collider, then attach the system on it: a hidden box still gives off its effect.
  • Per object (systems_set): effet (feu, fumee, etincelles, magie, pluie, neige, poussiere, eclats, eclats_bois, eclats_pierre, explosion, impact), taille (1 a campfire, 0.4 a torch; for rain and snow, the width of the area), teinte (effet, or choisie with couleur "#rrggbb": a blue fire), quantite (the number of particles, multiplied), boucle (true: runs while the object is there; false: plays once at the start), duree (seconds; 0 endless when looping), hauteur (metres above the object's base: the tip of a torch).
  • Fire, explosion, magic, sparks and hit give their own light: it follows the effect, flickers with a fire, grows with taille, and goes out with the effect. Fire, explosion and magic cast shadows from it (a crate next to a campfire casts its shadow); the object carrying the effect does not. « lumiere »: effet (default: its light, with its shadows), sans_ombres (the light alone, lighter to draw), aucune (no light). « force_lumiere »: multiplied (0.5 a discreet glow, 2 a blaze). Never add a placed light next to a fire made with this system: it already lights. These lights count with the placed lights (the closest first) and follow the shadow quality (world_set environment shadowQuality); they change nothing in the game, only the image.
  • On a visible object, the effect stops while the object is hidden and comes back when it is shown; destroyed, it stops. game.object_effect(id, false) puts it out, game.object_effect(id, true) lights it again; the Trigger does the same with « Jouer un effet » (effet « objet ») and « Arrêter un effet ».
  • Rain or snow over the whole game: place the system on the player, effet pluie or neige, taille 1 to 2: it follows them.
  • A one-off effect from a script, at a place or on an object: game.effect("explosion", pos), game.effect("eclats", rock) (chips take the rock's colour). See the script reference.
  • What the engine already does: a little dust when the player lands (landingDust of the player), chips and dust when an object bursts or collapses (game.effect(id, "burst")), dust where a falling object lands. The Gathering system sends chips at each hit, and the Combat system a hit impact; each has a setting to turn them off.
  • Effects follow the graphics quality, on three levels (High, Medium, Low: 6,000, 3,000 and 1,500 particles at once; fewer and slightly larger particles given off, simpler light on smoke at lower levels). An effect never breaks the game, it only looks lighter. A game run by the agent keeps High, so its report does not depend on the machine; the report gives the level under particles.quality and particles.budget.
  • The fire preset already has its flames, a bright core, a warm glow, embers and smoke: do not stack several fire effects to make one campfire, raise taille or quantite instead. In the editor, a visible effect animates on its own (30 frames per second in the active view, 10 in the others).

items.title: Passage (passage)
items.text:
Leads to another scene of the game: a door into a house, a cave entrance, the exit of a level. Activating it activates the interaction module; placing it on an object places interaction there too.

  • A game with several places has one scene per place, in the project's scenes folder. A scene's name is its file name, without folder or extension.
  • Place it on the door, the entrance or a zone (systems_attach), and set (systems_set): scene (where it leads, a name from scenes_list), arrivee (the name of an arrival point of that scene, where the player appears turned like it: entities_create with arrival: true, just inside the door), en_marchant (true: taken by walking into it within distance, without a key; false: with the interaction key).
  • Make the way back too: a passage in the other scene, leading to an arrival point just outside the first door. An arrival on a passage taken by walking does not send the player back at once (they must step out first), but keep them apart: the player would be standing in a doorway.
  • scene_validate lists passages that lead to a missing scene or arrival.
  • The player keeps everything (inventory, health, quests): scripts keep running. A scene left stays as it was.
  • From a script: game.go_to(scene, arrival?), and game.on("scene.change", function(e) ... end) with e.depuis and e.vers.

items.title: Physics
items.text:
The objects that carry it fall, roll, slide, and the player pushes them by walking into them: crates, barrels, a ball, rocks. Those that come at the player push back, by their mass: a rock knocks them aside, a ball bounces off. In water, they float, sink or stay in between, and drift with the water. Their shape wraps the model, or follows its outline. Placed on a folder, it applies to everything inside.

Identifier physique Version 3 Placed on objects yes Run by the engine yes: the engine runs it itself, without a script

Higher, they move heavier objects; 0: they push nothing. force_du_joueur Number 300 from 0 to 100 000

The first four are simple, at the model's size: a box slides and tips over, a ball rolls in every direction, a cylinder rolls on its side like a barrel, a capsule (a cylinder with rounded ends) rolls too, and tips over gently. The hull follows the model's outline, without its hollows: a rock rolls and catches on its edges, a statue stands on its base. It takes a little more computing: keep it for objects whose shape matters. forme Choice in a list Box: a crate, furniture boite: Box: a crate, furnitureboule: Ball: a ball, a round rockcylindre: Cylinder: a barrel, a columncapsule: Capsule: a bottle, a log, a dummyenveloppe: Model hull: its real outline (a rock, a statue) Mass (kg): the heavier, the harder to push Its weight, in kilograms: a crate 10 to 30, a barrel 40, a rock 200. The heavier, the harder to push. masse Number 10 from 0.1 to 100 000 Friction: 0 slides as on ice How much it grips the ground: 0 slides as on ice, 0.6 is ordinary friction, 1 and above grips hard. frottement Number 0.6 from 0 to 2 Bounce: 0 does not bounce, 1 bounces without losing anything How much it bounces when falling or hitting something: 0 does not bounce, like a crate; 0.8 bounces a lot, like a ball. rebond Number 0.1 from 0 to 1 In water What it does in the water of a lake or the sea. It floats half sunk, sinks slowly to the bottom, or stays in between. In every case, the water slows it down, rocks it with the waves and carries it along when it moves. Its pieces, if it breaks, do the same. eau Choice in a list Floats: a crate, a barrel, a ball flotte: Floats: a crate, a barrel, a ballentre_deux: In between: stays where it is let gocoule: Sinks: a stone, an anchor, an iron chestdensite: By its density, chosen below Density (kg per m³; water: 1,000)shown only if In water is “By its density, chosen below” How much one cubic meter of its material weighs, in kilograms. Less than water (1,000), it floats, the higher the lighter it is: wood 500, cork 200, ice 900. More, it sinks: stone 2,500, iron 7,800. densite Number 500 from 10 to 20 000 Drag in water (1 ordinary) How much the water slows it down and carries it: 1 is ordinary, 0 glides on the water without being held, 3 sticks to the water like a dead leaf. freinage_eau Number 1 from 0 to 10

items.title: Physics (physique)
items.text:
The objects carrying this system are simulated by the engine: they fall, roll, slide, bounce, and the player and characters push them by walking into them. Crates, barrels, balls, rocks, a cart. The system has no script: the engine does it all.

  • Make objects movable: modules_add it once, then systems_attach on each object, or on a group so that all its children move. An object carrying it does not need a collider: it collides by itself.
  • Per object (systems_set): forme, masse in kg (a crate 10 to 30, a barrel 40, a rock 200: the heavier, the harder to push), frottement (0 slides as on ice, 0.6 by default), rebond (0 to 1).
  • forme: boite (a crate, furniture: slides and tips over), boule (a ball, a round rock: rolls every way), cylindre (a barrel, a column: rolls on its side), capsule (a cylinder with rounded ends: a bottle, a log, a dummy; rolls on its side and tips over gently), all four at the size of the model; or enveloppe, the model's own outline without its hollows (a jagged rock that rolls and catches on its edges, a statue standing on its base, an L-shaped piece of furniture). enveloppe costs a little more: use it when the shape changes how the object moves, not for crates and balls. A flat model (a sign, a sheet) has no outline and becomes a boite.
  • A moving object hits the player and the characters as two bodies do, by their masses (a character weighs 70 kg): a 200 kg rock rolling down a slope knocks the player back, a 40 kg barrel shoves them a little, a light ball bounces off them. It never goes through them. To make a rolling trap dangerous, give it mass and speed (game.push); add damage with a zone on its path or a script, not by expecting the shove to hurt.
  • In water (a lake, the sea): « eau » says what it does. « flotte » (the default: half sunk, a crate, a barrel, a ball), « entre_deux » (stays at the depth where it is let go), « coule » (sinks slowly to the bottom: a stone, an anchor), or « densite » with densite in kg per m³ (below 1000 it floats, higher the lighter: cork 200, wood 500, ice 900; above, it sinks: stone 2500). « freinage_eau » (1 ordinary, 0 glides, 3 sticks to the water). The water slows it, rocks it with the waves and carries it when it moves; its pieces, if it breaks, float or sink like it.
  • For the whole game: force_du_joueur, the force in newtons with which the player and characters push (300 by default; 0: they never push anything).
  • Place them resting on the ground or on each other (entities_ground): one placed in the air falls when the game starts.
  • Scripts move them with the physics: game.push(id, vec(...)) throws one (a change of speed in m/s), game.velocity(id) reads its speed, game.set_position puts one back at rest. One that falls out of the world disappears.
  • To know when something reaches a place (a ball in a goal, a crate on a plate), use the zone system.
  • game_run reports moving_objects: how far each one travelled, and whether it fell out of the world. Check there that what should move did. Its « water » part lists each object that touched the water: « state » at the end (« floating », « underwater », « out_of_water »), « submerged_pct », « below_surface_m », « in_water_s » and « drift_m » (how far the water carried it); « floating_debris » counts broken pieces that floated.

items.title: Quest log
items.text:
The game's quests and their steps, which move on by themselves: on an event (a Trigger rule, a Dialogue answer, an enemy defeated), a Dialogue mark, items carried or items handed over. A finished quest can give a reward; a quest can also fail (an event, a mark, time running out) or be abandoned from the log, then be taken up again. A log opens with J, and a notification announces each new quest, each step and each end.

Identifier quetes Version 5 Placed on objects no

A quest starts when the game starts, on an event, a mark or the end of another; it ends when all its steps are done. It can also fail, or be abandoned by the player. quetes List of “Row” (empty) one line per “Row”: its fields Log with a key (J) Ticked: the Open the quest log control (J, or → on a gamepad) opens a window with the quests in progress, their steps, and the finished ones. The same key closes it. fenetre Yes or no yes Stop the game while the log is open Ticked: the world stops while the log is open. Unticked: the game goes on behind it, enemies included. pause_fenetre Yes or no yes Announce quests and steps on screen Ticked: a small message at the top of the screen announces a new quest, a step done and a finished quest, with its reward. notifications Yes or no yes Duration of an announcement (s) How many seconds of play each announcement stays on screen. items.text:
They appear in the Game tab, Controls section, where you can change their key.

Control Name for scripts Key Gamepad Open the quest log journal J →

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description quetes.debut quete (text) A quest started: quete is its title. quetes.etape quete (text), etape (number), texte (text) A step of a quest is done: etape is its rank in the quest (from 1), texte what it said. Sent before quetes.fin when it was the last one. quetes.fin quete (text) A quest is finished: all its steps are done. Its reward, if any, has been asked to the inventory. quetes.echec quete (text) A quest failed: an event, a mark, its time ran out, or quetes.echouer. It gives no reward; it may be given again if its settings allow it. quetes.abandon quete (text) The player abandoned a quest from the log (or quetes.abandonner asked for it). It gives no reward; it may be given again if its settings allow it. inventaire.ajouter objet (text), quantite (number), joueur (id?) Ask the inventory to add items, such as a reward. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.plein. With several players, joueur says whose bag; without it, the player whose action is being handled, or every player. inventaire.retirer objet (text), quantite (number) Ask the inventory to remove items, such as a payment. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.manque if there are not enough. dialogue.marquer marque (text), retirer (boolean?) Ask the dialogue system to set a mark, from a script or another system; with retirer true, to remove it. Dialogue conditions then see it.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description quetes.demarrer quete (text) Ask the quest log to give a quest to the player, by its title: from a script, a dialogue or a trigger. Nothing happens if it was already given. quetes.echouer quete (text) Ask the quest log to make a quest in progress fail, by its title: from a script or a trigger. Nothing happens if it is not in progress. quetes.abandonner quete (text) Ask the quest log to abandon a quest in progress, by its title, as the player does from the log. Nothing happens if it is not in progress. inventaire.change objet (text), quantite (number), total (number), chargement (boolean?) The quantity of an item changed. total is the new quantity. chargement is true when a saved game gives the items back (game.load): nothing was picked up. dialogue.marque marque (text) A dialogue set a mark: a word the game remembers (a line shown, an answer chosen). Every dialogue's conditions can use it. hud.clic cible (text), joueur (id?) A button of the HUD was clicked: pressed, then released on it; or chosen with A (Enter) while it has the gamepad or keyboard focus; or the window's back button (back = true), with B (Escape). cible is the button's key (game.hud_button), joueur the player who clicked (a guest clicks on their own computer; the host plays the click). Announced by the engine, before the scripts' on_update of that step.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • quetes.texte: function(default, key) -> the text the quest log shows for that key: titre, aucune, en_cours, terminees, fermer, fait, nouvelle, etape, finie, recompense, echouee, abandonnee, ratees, echouee_court, abandonnee_court, abandonner, confirmer, reste, manque. It may hold {quete}, {etape}, {objet}, {n} and {total}, replaced afterwards (in the player's language). The default is the game's translation of the text in the original language (translations_get lists them as built-in texts of the quest log); without one, French or English, after the player's language.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Quest log (quetes)
items.text:
The game's quests and their steps, written in its settings and moved on by events, without code. A notification announces each new quest, step done and quest finished; the current step shows on the right of the screen; a log window opens with the control journal (J, or → on a gamepad). Add it once with modules_add; it is for the whole game, not placed on objects. Use it whenever the user talks about quests, missions, objectives or tasks to do: do not write a quest script.

Its game setting quetes (modules_set) is a list of rows, in order. A quete row starts a quest; the etape rows under it are its steps.

  • quete: titre (shown, and names the quest in events), description, depart (when the player gets it):
  • debut: when the game starts;
  • evenement: on the event depart_evenement, such as an answer of a dialogue with annonce: "loups.accepte", or a declencheur rule "send an event";
  • marque: when the Dialogue mark depart_marque is set (at once if it already is);
  • quete: when the quest titled depart_quete ends: a chain of quests. Also dans_l_ordre (on: one step after the other, the next ones hidden in the log; off: all at once), recompense and recompense_quantite (items the inventory receives at the end; needs inventaire). Failing, echec (what makes the quest in progress fail; no reward then):
  • aucun: never (the default);
  • evenement: the event echec_evenement happens while the quest is in progress, about an object named echec_cible if given (sante.mort with "Marchand": the merchant to escort died);
  • marque: the Dialogue mark echec_marque is set (at once if it already is);
  • temps: echec_delai seconds of play pass after its start (time waits during a pause; the tracker and the log show what is left, such as "Reste 0:42"). abandon (on by default: the log shows an Abandonner button under it, pressed twice), reprendre (on by default: what gives the quest gives it again, from the start, after it failed or was abandoned; a quest that starts with the game is only given again by « quetes.demarrer »), marque_echec and annonce_echec (a mark and an event when it fails or is abandoned: the miller complains).
  • etape: texte (what to do, as the log writes it), and fin (what ends it):
  • evenement: the event fin_evenement happens fin_fois times while the step is active; fin_cible keeps only events about an object of that name ("Loup" counts "Loup 1", "Loup 2"). For example sante.mort with fin_cible "Loup" and fin_fois 5 (five wolves defeated), dialogue.fin with fin_cible "Meunier" (a talk with the miller finished), zone.entree with the zone's name (a place reached), boutique.achat, collecte.recolte, or an event the game names itself;
  • marque: the Dialogue mark fin_marque is set (at once if it already is);
  • objet: the player carries fin_quantite of fin_objet at the same time (from the inventory; done at once if they already do);
  • remettre: on the event fin_evenement (for fin_cible if given, such as dialogue.fin with "Meunier"), if the player carries fin_quantite of fin_objet, the inventory takes them back and the step is done; otherwise an announcement says how many are missing, and the step waits for the next time. Use it for "Bring 3 pelts to the miller".
  • On both: marque (a mark set when it ends, which every dialogue's tests and answers see) and annonce (an event sent when it ends, for a declencheur rule: a bridge appears, a door opens).

A quest is finished when all its steps are done. Write every title and step in the user's language, and keep steps short.

A miller who asks to hunt wolves, then thanks the player:

  1. Miller's dialogue: an answer "I'll do it" with annonce: "loups.accepte", marque: "loups_acceptes"; a test on the mark loups_chasses leads to a thank-you line with an answer "Here they are" whose annonce is loups.rendus.
  2. quetes: {"sorte": "quete", "titre": "Les loups du moulin", "depart": "evenement", "depart_evenement": "loups.accepte", "recompense": "Or", "recompense_quantite": 50}, then {"sorte": "etape", "texte": "Vaincre 3 loups", "fin": "evenement", "fin_evenement": "sante.mort", "fin_cible": "Loup", "fin_fois": 3, "marque": "loups_chasses"}, then {"sorte": "etape", "texte": "Revenir voir le meunier", "fin": "evenement", "fin_evenement": "loups.rendus"}.

Other details:

  • Events announced: quetes.debut (quete: its title), quetes.etape (quete, etape: its rank, texte), quetes.fin (quete), quetes.echec (quete) and quetes.abandon (quete). A declencheur rule or a script can react to them; for one particular quest, prefer its annonce or annonce_echec.
  • Give a quest from a script: game.emit("quetes.demarrer", {quete = "Les loups du moulin"}); make it fail or abandon it: game.emit("quetes.echouer", {quete = ...}), game.emit("quetes.abandonner", {quete = ...}). A step can also end on an event your script sends.
  • Game settings: fenetre (the log with J), pause_fenetre (the world stops while it is open), notifications and duree_notification (seconds), suivi (the current step on the right of the screen, with its progress such as 2/5). Notifications and the step on screen hide during a pause (a menu, a dialogue, a shop).
  • Texts follow the player's language. The log's own texts (Quest log, New quest...) are built-in texts of the system, listed by translations_get with the game's texts: translate them there for every language the game offers (French and English are built in). Quest titles, descriptions, step texts and rewards are translated with the game's tables too; events keep the original title, so depart_quete and quetes.demarrer name a quest by its original title. To change a word, override quetes.texte from a game script: game.override("quetes.texte", function(default, key) if key == "titre" then return "Missions" end return default(key) end). Keys and their {quete}, {etape}, {objet}, {n} placeholders are in modules_info.
  • Saved games: game.save keeps every quest's state (failed and abandoned ones included), its steps done, its counts (2 wolves out of 3), the time left to a timed quest and the marks; game.load gives them back, without announcing the quests again. Nothing to write.
  • Gamepad and keyboard: B or Escape closes the log (quetes.fermer is its back button), like A or Enter on Close. The Abandonner buttons (quetes.abandonner.<n>, n the quest's rank among the quest rows) are reached like any other button.
  • HUD keys start with quetes.: do not use that prefix in a game script.
  • Testing: in game_run, do what each step asks, then press journal and read the report's hud (quetes.l.<n>, quetes.suivi.titre, quetes.suivi.reste); game.log in a script listening to quetes.etape shows the order.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One copy per player: each player has their own quests, steps, journal and rewards (into their own bag).
