items.title: Health
items.text:
Health and armor for the objects that carry it: the player, a group of skeletons, a boss, each with its own values. Shows nothing: add "Health bar" to see it.

Identifier sante Version 6 Placed on objects yes

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Game tab, Systems section, by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Armor calculation How armor reduces damage, in the whole game. Simple: an armor of 25 stops 25 % of each hit (90 % at most). Curve: armor is counted in points, each one counting a little less than the one before, for a role-playing game with a long progression. calcul Choice in a list Simple: armor is a percentage pourcentage: Simple: armor is a percentagecourbe: Curve: armor / (armor + K), like Diablo or WoW Curve: the armor that stops half the damage (K) With the curve calculation: the armor that stops half the damage. With 100, an armor of 100 stops half, 300 stops three quarters. constante Number 100 from 1 to 1 000 000

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Health points Its health at the start of the game, which is also its maximum health. At zero, it dies. points_de_vie Number 100 from 1 to 1 000 000 Armor (in % or in points, depending on the game's calculation) What reduces each hit taken. With the simple calculation, a percentage: 25 stops 25 %. With the curve calculation, points: see the game setting. armure Number 0 from 0 to 1 000 000 Invulnerability after a hit (s) After a hit, it loses no health for this many seconds: hits too close together count only once. 0: every hit counts. invulnerabilite Number 0.5 from 0 to 60 Remove the object when it dies (not the player) Ticked: the object leaves the game when it dies. Unticked: it stays there. The player is never removed. detruire_a_la_mort Yes or no no

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description sante.change cible (id), vie (number), max (number) An object's health changed, or is announced once when the game starts. sante.mort cible (id), source (id?) An object's health reached zero. What happens next belongs to the game: the health module does nothing else, unless its setting says to destroy the object. sante.pare cible (id), source (id?), montant (number) A hit was blocked by a guard: montant is the damage it stopped. For a clang, sparks, a stamina cost.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description scene.change depuis (text), vers (text) Sent by the engine once the player has arrived in another scene of the game (game.go_to, or a passage). Scripts keep running across scenes: this is when a module looks at the objects of the new scene. sante.blesser cible (id), montant (number), source (id?) Ask the health module to remove health from an object. sante.soigner cible (id), montant (number) Ask the health module to give health back, up to its maximum. sante.garde cible (id), part (number), angle (number) An object protects itself, or stops (part 0): hits coming from in front of it, within angle degrees, lose part of their damage (0 to 1) before its armor. A hit without a source cannot be blocked.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • sante.degats: function(default, cible, brut, source, retenue) -> the health removed. brut: the raw damage sent; retenue: the share stopped by the target's armor (0 to 1). The default returns brut * (1 - retenue). For critical hits, weaknesses, a boss that only takes fire.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Health (sante)
items.text:
Health and armor for the objects that carry this system: place it on the player, on an enemy, or on a group so that all its children have it. Each object or group has its own values: an early skeleton and a final boss do not have the same health. It decides nothing for the game: it removes and gives back health, and announces changes and deaths.

  • Place it with systems_attach, and set each group's values with systems_set: points_de_vie, armure, invulnerabilite, detruire_a_la_mort. A child can change one value for itself; the rest comes from its group.
  • For the whole game (modules_set): calcul is pourcentage (armor 25 stops 25 % of each hit, at most 90 %) or courbe (armor in points, stopping armor / (armor + K): with K = constante = 100, 100 armor stops half, 300 stops 75 %). Choose courbe for an RPG with a long progression; tell the user.
  • Hurt something: game.emit("sante.blesser", {cible = id, montant = 10, source = attacker}). montant is the raw damage: the target's armor is applied here.
  • Heal: game.emit("sante.soigner", {cible = id, montant = 10}). For potions, food and springs, use the module soins.
  • Guard: game.emit("sante.garde", {cible = id, part = 0.7, angle = 120}) makes hits from in front lose 70 % before armor, until sent again with part = 0. The player's blocking comes from combat.basique: use this only for a guard of your own, such as a shielded enemy. Announced by sante.pare.
  • This module shows nothing on screen. For the player's health bar, add barre_de_vie; for anything else, listen to sante.change (cible, vie, max). It is announced once for everyone on the first step, then on each change.
  • React to a death: listen to sante.mort (cible, source). What a death means (game over, loot, respawn) belongs to the game, and only if the user asked for it.
  • Objects cloned during the game from an object carrying it have its values.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One for the whole game: every object carrying it has its own health, each player's character included. A player is never destroyed at death.

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/sante/module.json, modules/sante/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Healing
items.text:
What carries this system gives health back to the player: a spring to touch, or a potion picked up into the inventory and drunk with a key, each with what it gives.

Identifier soins Version 3 Placed on objects yes Also activates Health

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Game tab, Systems section, by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Heal by walking over (what does not go to the inventory) Ticked: an object that heals on the spot, without going to the inventory (a spring, a heart), heals as soon as the player walks over it. Unticked: it must be used, if it also carries the Interaction system. au_contact Yes or no yes Reach to touch (m) The distance, in meters, at which the player touches an object that heals by walking over it. distance_contact Number 1.2 from 0.1 to 10 Action to drink a potion from the inventory The game's control action that drinks a potion carried ("heal": R by default, ↑ on a gamepad). The player drinks the first kind of potion they have. action Text heal Time between two potions (s) The minimum time, in seconds, between two potions drunk: longer, the player cannot drink them all at once in the middle of a fight. recharge Number 1 from 0 to 60 Use nothing up when health is full Ticked: when the player's health is full, no potion is drunk and no object disappears for nothing. vie_pleine Yes or no yes

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Health given The health points this object gives back to the player, without going past their maximum health. montant Number 30 from 0 to 1 000 000 Comes back after (s, 0: never) For an object that heals on the spot: it comes back after this many seconds. 0: it is gone for good. An arena whose healing comes back keeps a long fight playable. reapparition Number 0 from 0 to 3600

items.title: Controls added to the game
items.text:
They appear in the Game tab, Controls section, where you can change their key.

Control Name for scripts Key Gamepad Drink a potion heal R ↑

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description soins.soin cible (id), montant (number), objet (text) The healing module gave health back: a potion drunk, a spring touched. objet is the kind of potion or the name of what healed. sante.soigner cible (id), montant (number) Ask the health module to give health back, up to its maximum. inventaire.retirer objet (text), quantite (number) Ask the inventory to remove items, such as a payment. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.manque if there are not enough.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description scene.change depuis (text), vers (text) Sent by the engine once the player has arrived in another scene of the game (game.go_to, or a passage). Scripts keep running across scenes: this is when a module looks at the objects of the new scene. sante.change cible (id), vie (number), max (number) An object's health changed, or is announced once when the game starts. interaction.utiliser cible (id), joueur (id) The player used the object in reach: a door, a merchant, an item to pick up. Whoever owns that object decides what it does. inventaire.change objet (text), quantite (number), total (number), chargement (boolean?) The quantity of an item changed. total is the new quantity. chargement is true when a saved game gives the items back (game.load): nothing was picked up.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Healing (soins)
items.text:
Objects carrying this system give health back to the player, each with its own montant (systems_set). Activating it activates the health module. Use it whenever the player can be hurt and fights last: without a way to heal, a long fight is lost in advance.

  • Picked up and drunk later (potions, food): place inventaire on the object too. It is picked up like any item, under its kind (the inventory's nom, or its name without a trailing number; a kind renamed by overriding inventaire.sorte is not seen here, so set nom instead). The action heal (R by default, ↑ on a gamepad) drinks the first kind carried and gives that kind's montant. recharge is the time between two.
  • Used on the spot (a spring, a heart, a campfire): no inventory. It heals when the player walks over it (game setting au_contact, on by default), or when used if it also carries interaction. Then it is removed, or comes back after reapparition seconds: an arena whose healing comes back keeps a long fight possible.
  • With vie_pleine on (the default), nothing is used up while the player's health is full.
  • Each heal is announced by soins.soin (cible, montant, objet): listen to it for a sound or an effect. Health bars follow on their own (sante.change).
  • Name potions and food in the user's language. Do not heal from your own script with sante.soigner when this module fits.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One copy per player: what a player touches or drinks heals that player.

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/soins/module.json, modules/soins/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Sounds
items.text:
The game's noises, placed on what makes them: footsteps of characters (timed by their animation, and by the ground), hits given and taken, deaths, doors and chests being used, ambience of a fire or a river, an enemy's alert cry. Plus, for the whole game: music, fight music, pickups. Several files separated by commas: a random one each time.

Identifier sons Version 8 Placed on objects yes

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Game tab, Systems section, by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Background music (loops from the start) The music looping from the start of the game. Several files separated by commas: a random one. musique Text (empty) Fight music (while an enemy chases the player) The music that replaces the background music while an enemy chases the player; the background music then fades back in. Empty: the background music keeps playing. musique_combat Text (empty) Music volume The music volume: 0 silent, 1 loudest. 0.5 keeps it under the game's noises. volume_musique Number 0.5 from 0 to 1 Item picked up (Inventory module) The sound played when the player picks something up (Inventory system). Several files separated by commas: a random one. ramassage Text (empty) Inventory full The sound played when the player can no longer pick up a new kind of item: their inventory is full. inventaire_plein Text (empty) Healing (potion drunk, spring touched: Healing module) The sound played at each heal of the Healing system: a potion drunk, a spring touched. soin Text (empty) Player exhausted (Stamina module) The sound played when the player runs out of stamina (Stamina system). essoufflement Text (empty) Sound mixer group: noises (steps, hits, deaths, doors, gathering, healing) The sound mixer group (Game tab, Sound mixer section) the game's noises go to: steps, hits, blocks, deaths, alerts, doors, gathering, healing, exhaustion. Its volume sets them all at once. groupe_bruits Group of the sound mixer effects Sound mixer group: looping ambiences (fire, river) The sound mixer group the looping ambiences placed on objects go to: a fire, a river, a forge. Lower it to push them into the background. groupe_ambiance Group of the sound mixer ambience Sound mixer group: cues (item picked up, inventory full) The sound mixer group the small cues that come from nowhere in particular go to: an item picked up, the inventory full. groupe_interface Group of the sound mixer ui Pitch variation for each sound (0: always the same) Slightly changes the pitch of each sound, so that twenty identical steps do not sound mechanical. 0: always the same; 0.08: barely; 0.3: very varied. variation Number 0.08 from 0 to 0.5

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Footsteps (timed by the walk and run animation) This character's footsteps. With a walk or run animation, each step falls when a foot touches the ground. Give two to four files separated by commas for variety. pas Text (empty) Steps on this object (a floor, a bridge: replaces those of whoever walks on it) To place on a floor, a bridge, a carpet: whoever walks on it makes these steps instead of their own. The floor needs a collider. surface Text (empty) Without animation: distance between two steps when walking (m) For what moves without animation: one step every so many meters walked. When running, the stride gets longer, up to double. foulee Number 0.8 from 0.2 to 5 Footstep volume The footstep volume, compared with the other sounds of this object: 0 silent, 1 just as loud. volume_pas Number 0.6 from 0 to 1 Jump (the player) The sound played when the player jumps. Only used on the player. saut Text (empty) Landing after a jump or a fall (the player) The sound played when the player lands after a jump or a fall. atterrissage Text (empty) Strike, hit or miss (the weapon's swing) The sound of its weapon, played at each strike, whether it hits or not (Combat system). attaque Text (empty) Hit taken The sound played when it takes a hit, from the player or an enemy. coup_recu Text (empty) Hit blocked (the shield or blade sound) The sound played when it blocks a hit: the shield or blade stopping it. parade Text (empty) Death The sound played when it dies (Health system). mort Text (empty) Alert (an enemy starts chasing) The sound played when this enemy spots the player and starts chasing them. alerte Text (empty) When used (door, chest, lever: Interaction module) The sound played when the player uses it: a door, a chest, a lever (Interaction system). utiliser Text (empty) Gathering: each hit (axe in wood, pick in stone: Gathering module) The sound of each hit on this resource: the axe in wood, the pick in stone (Gathering system). recolte_coup Text (empty) Gathering: when used up (a tree falling, a rock bursting) The sound played when this resource is used up: a tree falling, a rock bursting. It stays where the resource was, even if it disappears. recolte_fin Text (empty) Looping ambience (fire, river, forge) A looping sound coming from this object: a fire, a river, a forge. Only the eight ambiences nearest the player play at the same time. ambiance Text (empty) Group of its sounds in the sound mixer (Automatic: by kind of sound) The sound mixer group all this object's sounds go to: Voice for a talking character, Ambience for a radio. Automatic: its noises go with the noises, its ambience with the ambiences. groupe Group of the sound mixer (empty) Volume of its sounds The volume of all this object's sounds: 0 silent, 1 loudest. They also get quieter with distance. volume Number 1 from 0 to 1 Range: beyond it, it is not heard (m) The distance, in meters, beyond which its sounds are no longer heard: 25 m for a character, more for a waterfall, less for a small fire. portee Number 25 from 2 to 300

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description scene.change depuis (text), vers (text) Sent by the engine once the player has arrived in another scene of the game (game.go_to, or a passage). Scripts keep running across scenes: this is when a module looks at the objects of the new scene. combat.attaque source (id) Someone struck, whether it hit or not: the stamina module counts it. combat.coup cible (id), source (id), montant (number) An attack hit something. The health module, if present, has been asked to remove the damage. sante.mort cible (id), source (id?) An object's health reached zero. What happens next belongs to the game: the health module does nothing else, unless its setting says to destroy the object. interaction.utiliser cible (id), joueur (id) The player used the object in reach: a door, a merchant, an item to pick up. Whoever owns that object decides what it does. collecte.coup cible (id), coups (number), restants (number) The player hit a resource (a use of something carrying collecte). restants is how many hits are left before it is used up. collecte.epuise cible (id) A resource is used up and is about to disappear (destroyed, or hidden until it grows back): it still exists while this is sent. inventaire.change objet (text), quantite (number), total (number), chargement (boolean?) The quantity of an item changed. total is the new quantity. chargement is true when a saved game gives the items back (game.load): nothing was picked up. inventaire.plein objet (text) An item could not be added: every slot holds another kind of item. ennemi.etat cible (id), etat (text) An enemy changed state: patrouille (patrols), poursuite (chases the player), attaque (hits in reach), attente (waits its turn near the player, when enough others are already striking), retour (goes back to its spot), mort (dead, does nothing more). endurance.change valeur (number), max (number), epuise (boolean) The player's stamina changed. epuise is true from zero until they regain a share of it: meanwhile they cannot run, jump or strike. sante.pare cible (id), source (id?), montant (number) A hit was blocked by a guard: montant is the damage it stopped. For a clang, sparks, a stamina cost. soins.soin cible (id), montant (number), objet (text) The healing module gave health back: a potion drunk, a spring touched. objet is the kind of potion or the name of what healed.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • sons.pas: function(default, id, sol, fichiers) -> the files of this footstep (text, commas allowed), or "" for silence. sol: the object under the feet or nil; fichiers: what the module would play (the ground's surface, or the walker's steps).

items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Sounds (sons)
items.text:
The game's noises, placed on what makes them, like the other systems: on the player, on a folder of skeletons, on a door, on a campfire. Each object or folder has its own sounds. Only with sound files the user has: find them with assets_search and kind sound.

  • Placed on objects (systems_attach, then systems_set): pas (footsteps: for animated characters, each one falls when a foot touches the ground in the walk or run animation, at any speed; foulee in metres only serves objects without animation), surface (placed on a floor, a bridge, a carpet: whoever walks on it makes these steps instead of their own), saut and atterrissage (the player's jump and landing), attaque (the swing of its weapon, hit or miss), coup_recu, parade (a hit it blocked), mort, alerte (an enemy starts chasing), utiliser (a door, a chest, a lever used through the interaction module), ambiance (a loop coming from it: fire, river, forge; only the nearest play), plus volume, portee (beyond it, not heard), foulee, volume_pas.
  • For the whole game (modules_set): musique, musique_combat (while an enemy chases the player), volume_musique, ramassage, inventaire_plein, soin (a heal from the module soins), essoufflement, variation (a slightly different pitch each time, so twenty identical sounds do not sound mechanical).
  • Sound mixer groups: its noises (steps, hits, deaths, doors, gathering, heals) go to groupe_bruits (effects), the looping ambiences to groupe_ambiance (ambience), pickups and a full inventory to groupe_interface (ui), the music to music. On an object, groupe sends all its sounds to one group (voice for a talking character, ambience for a radio); empty: by kind of sound. Balance whole groups with mixer_set, not each object's volume.
  • Several files separated by commas give a random one each time: give footsteps and hits two to four files when the pack has them.
  • It only listens to what the other modules announce: hits and swings come from combat.basique and ennemis, deaths from sante, uses from interaction, pickups from inventaire. A sound the game needs elsewhere (a lever in a puzzle, a cutscene) is a game.sound in that script.
  • Different grounds: place the module on each kind of floor (or its folder) with surface: grass, stone, wood. The floor needs a collider. A character still needs the module on itself to make steps at all.
  • In game_run nothing is heard: the report's sounds lists what played.

items.title: Several players
items.text: One for the whole game, what the host hears: sounds placed somewhere (steps, hits, jumps of every player) are heard from everyone; sounds with no place (picking up, running out of breath) are the host's only. Guests do not hear the game's sounds yet.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
Its sounds reach the guests: the sounds placed somewhere (steps, hits, jumps of every player) and the music are heard by everyone, each from their own place; a sound without a place for one player (picking up, getting out of breath) is heard by that player only.

items.title: Vehicle
items.text:
Turns a model into a car, a motorbike or a boat you drive. A car: its wheels (chosen among its children, found by their name, or taken out of a one-piece model) spin, steer and follow the suspension. A motorbike: it stays upright, leans into turns and can fall over. A boat: its hull floats, measured on its model, an engine pushes it and a rudder turns it; it runs aground on land. The player gets in and out with the Use control, drives with the game's controls, on the keyboard or the gamepad, and the camera follows.

Identifier vehicule Version 4 Placed on objects yes Run by the engine yes: the engine runs it itself, without a script

items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Kind of vehicle A car rolls on its wheels. A motorbike rolls on two wheels: it stays upright by itself, leans into turns and falls over if knocked down. A boat floats on its hull, measured on its model: an engine at the back pushes it, a rudder turns it, it rocks with the waves and runs aground on land. Place the boat on the water of a lake or the sea. sorte Choice in a list Car: wheels on land voiture: Car: wheels on landmoto: Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the otherbateau: Boat: a hull on water Wheels (empty: found by their name)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” The objects inside the vehicle that are its wheels. Empty: those whose name contains "roue", "wheel", "tire", "tyre" or "pneu". With no wheel found, the model's own wheels if it is made in one piece (see "Wheels of the model"), otherwise invisible wheels under the model (four at a car's corners, two in the middle of a motorbike). Their size comes from their model. roues List of “Wheel” (empty) one line per “Wheel”: its fields Wheels of a one-piece modelshown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” When no wheel is placed apart, looks for the wheels inside the model itself: the round pieces at its bottom, seen from the side. In the game, they come off and turn like real wheels. Unchecked: invisible wheels carry it, and the model's own wheels stay still. roues_du_modele Yes or no yes Lean in turns (degrees)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” How far the motorbike leans at most in a turn: 45 for a road bike, 55 for a racing bike, 25 for a scooter. The more it leans, the tighter it turns at high speed. inclinaison Number 45 from 0 to 70 Balance (1: ordinary)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” The strength that keeps the motorbike upright and straightens it after a turn: 1 ordinary, 2 very steady, 0.5 wobbly. equilibre Number 1 from 0.1 to 5 Handling (1: ordinary)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” How fast the handlebars turn when steering: 1 ordinary (a quarter of a second from one end to the other), 2 quick, 0.5 heavy. Too quick, a sharp turn can knock it down. maniabilite Number 1 from 0.1 to 5 Hit that unbalances it (m/s)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” Hit from the side (a rock, a car), the motorbike loses its balance for a moment if its sideways speed changes at once by more than this, in meters per second: the momentum knocks it down, or it recovers. 4 ordinary, 8 sturdy, 0: never. choc Number 4 from 0 to 50 Can fall overshown only if Kind of vehicle is “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” Checked: knocked over (a crash, a turn too tight), the motorbike falls on its side and the rider is thrown off; getting back on with the Use control sets it upright. Unchecked: it never leans further than its lean setting, as in an arcade game. chute Yes or no yes Front of the model The side of the model that is the front of the vehicle. A car's or a motorbike's wheels on that side steer; a boat's propeller is on the opposite side. An arrow shows it in the 3D view when the vehicle is selected. avant Choice in a list +Z (most models) +z: +Z (most models)-z: −Z+x: +X-x: −X Mass (kg) Its weight, in kilograms: a car 1,200, a kart 150, a truck 8,000, a motorbike 200, a scooter 110; a motorboat 1,200, a rowing boat 150. The heavier, the more it pushes what it hits and the more power it needs; a heavy boat sits deeper. masse Number 1200 from 10 to 100 000 Engine power (N·m)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” The engine's torque, in newton-meters: it makes it accelerate. 600 for a car, 150 for a kart or a motorbike, 3,000 for a truck. puissance Number 600 from 10 to 100 000 Top speed (km/h) Beyond it, it no longer speeds up, forwards or backwards, in kilometers per hour. vitesse_max Number 80 from 1 to 500 Grip (1: dry road)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” How much the tires grip: 1 on a dry road, 0.4 slides as on snow, 1.5 sticks like a race car. adherence Number 1 from 0.1 to 3 Suspension travel (m)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” How much each wheel moves up and down, in meters: 0.3 for a car, 0.6 for an off-roader. suspension Number 0.3 from 0.02 to 2 Suspension stiffnessshown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” 1.5 is soft like an everyday car, 3 is firm like a sports car; lower, it sways. raideur Number 1.5 from 0.2 to 10 Front wheel steering (degrees)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” How far the front wheels turn at full lock: 30 for a car; more, it turns tighter. braquage Number 30 from 0 to 70 Brake strength (N·m per wheel)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” The brake strength of each wheel. The hand brake (Jump: Space, or A on a gamepad) locks the rear wheels. freins Number 1500 from 0 to 100 000 Driving assist (1: arcade)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” 1, as in an arcade game: at speed it steers less, the wheel turns smoothly even on the keyboard, and it follows the road without spinning out or sliding sideways (the hand brake still makes it drift). 0: physics alone, like a simulation; 0.5 in between. aide Number 1 from 0 to 1 Visible drivershown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” Checked: the player's character stays on screen while driving, seated on the motorbike (astride, hands on the handlebars, leaning with it) or in the car (in the driver's seat, hands on the wheel). Unchecked: they disappear while driving, as in a car with tinted windows. conducteur Yes or no yes Driving animation (optional)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” An animation of the player's character, looped while driving. Empty: an animation whose name is about driving or sitting (drive, ride, sit, seat…), if their model has one; otherwise a seated pose made from their own. animation_conduite Player animation (empty) Seat: forwards (m)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” Moves the driver forwards (or backwards, negative), in meters, from the place measured on the model: a motorbike's saddle, a car's driver seat. siege_avant Number 0 from -5 to 5 Seat: upwards (m)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” Raises (or lowers, negative) the driver, in meters: when they sink into the saddle or float above it. siege_hauteur Number 0 from -3 to 3 Seat: to the right (m)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” Moves the driver to the right (or to the left, negative), in meters: a British car's wheel is on the right. siege_cote Number 0 from -3 to 3 Engine thrust (N)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Boat: a hull on water” The engine's force, in newtons: it makes it speed up. 4,000 for a 1,200 kg motorboat, 800 for a rowing boat, 40,000 for a fishing boat. The engine only pushes in water. poussee Number 4000 from 1 to 1 000 000 Turn at full rudder (degrees per second)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Boat: a hull on water” How far the boat turns in one second at full rudder, once moving: 40 for a motorboat, 15 for a big boat. The rudder turns better the faster the boat moves. virage Number 40 from 0 to 180

items.title: Vehicle (vehicule)
items.text:
Turns a model into a car, a motorbike or a boat the player drives: wheels with suspension, engine, brakes and steering. The engine runs it, without a script. The player gets in and out with the interact control (E, Y on a gamepad) next to it, drives with the movement controls (forward and back accelerate or brake then reverse, left and right steer), jump is the hand brake; the camera follows behind it.

  • systems_attach it on the car object itself (or on the folder that holds the body and the wheels), placed on the ground, not on each part.
  • Wheels: the car's children (any depth) whose name contains roue, wheel, tire, tyre or pneu are found by themselves; otherwise list them in roues ([{"objet": "<wheel id>"}, ...]). Their size and place come from their models. Never assume a pack's names: look at the children (entities_list) and list them if their names say nothing.
  • A model made in one piece (no wheel among its children): with « roues_du_modele » on (the default), the engine looks for the wheels inside the model itself, the round pieces at its bottom seen from the side; in the game they come off the body and turn like real wheels. The editor circles them when the vehicle is selected. When none is found (the wheels are welded to the body), invisible wheels carry it: four at a car's corners, two in the middle of a motorbike, and the model's own wheels do not turn.
  • avant: which side of the model is the front (+z most models, -z, +x, -x): the wheels on that side steer. Check it in a screenshot: an arrow shows it when the vehicle is selected.
  • Per object: masse (kg, car 1200, kart 150, motorbike 200), puissance (engine torque N·m: car 600, kart or motorbike 150, truck 3000), vitesse_max (km/h), adherence (1 dry road, 0.4 snow), suspension (travel in m), raideur (1.5 soft, 3 firm), braquage (degrees), freins. Game-wide: distance to get in.
  • A motorbike: set « sorte » to « moto ». Two wheels one behind the other (found or listed like a car's, the front one steers, the rear one drives). It stands upright by itself, parked or ridden, and leans into turns. Per object: « inclinaison » (the most it leans in a turn, degrees: 45 road bike, 55 racing, 25 scooter), « equilibre » (how hard it straightens, 1 ordinary), « maniabilite » (how fast the handlebars turn, 1 ordinary), « choc » (a sideways hit faster than this, in m/s, unbalances it for a moment: 4 ordinary, 0 never), « chute » (can fall over, on by default). Knocked over (a crash, a hard hit), it falls on its side and its rider is thrown off (a rider with the chiffon system falls limp); getting back on with interact or game.drive sets it upright. Set « masse » and « puissance » for a bike: the defaults are a car's.
  • Driving feel: « aide » (driving assist, 0 to 1, default 1) makes a car or a motorbike arcade-friendly, as in GTA or Forza Horizon: it steers less at speed (full lock standing, a third at 80 km/h), the steering moves smoothly even on the keyboard, and the vehicle follows where its wheels point, within its grip, instead of spinning out or sliding sideways (the hand brake still drifts). 0 is physics alone, like a simulation. When the user says a vehicle is hard to drive, check « aide » is 1 before touching anything else; a car that turns too little at speed: raise « braquage »; a motorbike that leans too little: raise « inclinaison ».
  • The driver stays visible (« conducteur », on by default): seated astride the motorbike, hands on the handlebars, leaning with it, or in the car's driver seat (left side), hands on the wheel, seen through the windows. The seat is measured on the model (a motorbike: the top of the model between the wheels; a car: driver side, a bit over a third of its height); « siege_avant », « siege_hauteur », « siege_cote » (meters) move it when the rider sinks into the saddle or floats above it: check a screenshot while driving. « animation_conduite »: a clip of the player's character looped while driving; empty, a clip whose name says drive, ride, sit or seat is used if the model has one (read animation_clips), otherwise a seated pose is made from the character's own. « conducteur » off hides the driver while driving (tinted windows). A boat's driver stays hidden.
  • Copies: game.clone(id, pos) of a vehicle gives another vehicle you can drive, with its wheels; a vehicle hidden then shown again (game.set_visible) is a vehicle again.
  • Scripts: game.drive(id) puts the player in, game.leave_vehicle(), game.driving() (the vehicle driven or nil), game.vehicle(id) (speed in km/h, driven, flipped, motorbike, fallen, lean in degrees). Events vehicule.monte and vehicule.descendu (cible, qui): a race starts when the player gets in; vehicule.tombe (cible, qui if someone rode it) when a motorbike falls over.
  • A zone detects the driven vehicle as the player: a finish line works as for a runner.
  • Check with game_run and inputs: press interact next to it, then hold move_forward; vehicles reports « kind » (car, motorbike, boat), top_speed_kmh, travelled_m, flipped (it turned over during the run) and driven_s, wheels, invisible_wheels and « model_wheels » (taken out of a one-piece model). A motorbike adds « max_lean_deg » (how far it leaned), « falls » and « fallen_now ». A vehicle that does not move: check its wheels are found and that it stands on the ground. A motorbike that falls at once: lower « maniabilite » or raise « equilibre ».
  • A boat: set « sorte » to « bateau » and place it on the water (a lake or the sea, its bottom at the surface). No wheels: its hull is measured on its model (length, width slice by slice, bottom), how deep it sits comes from masse, its center of gravity is at the waterline so a mast does not capsize it. Per object: masse (motorboat 1200, rowing boat 150), « poussee » (engine thrust in N: 4000 for a 1200 kg motorboat, 800 for a rowing boat), « vitesse_max » (km/h, it levels off there at full thrust), « virage » (degrees per second at full rudder, once moving: 40 motorboat, 15 big boat). Driven like a car; the engine only pushes in water, so it runs aground on land and stays there. It rocks with the waves and drifts with moving water.
  • For a boat, game_run's vehicles adds « kind » « boat », « afloat_s », « aground_now », « aground_s », « draft_m » (how deep its hull sits) and « float_points » (where the water carries it, measured on the model; 4 or more). game.vehicle(id) has boat and aground. A boat that does not move: check it is on the water (« afloat_s » above 0) and not « aground_now ».

items.title: Several players
items.text:
The engine runs it once for the whole game: any player gets in and out with interact, drives with their own controls, and nobody gets into a vehicle another player drives (vehicule.monte and vehicule.descendu carry joueur). Every player sees the others seated on the vehicles they drive.

items.title: Zone
items.text:
A zone that announces who enters and who leaves it: a pressure plate, a trap, a finish line, a goal. Place it on an invisible box, of the size you want. The game decides what happens.

Identifier zone Version 1 Placed on objects yes Run by the engine yes: the engine runs it itself, without a script

items.title: Zone (zone)
items.text:
An object carrying this system announces zone.entree and zone.sortie when something enters or leaves its box: the box of its model, at its place, rotation and scale. The system has no script: the engine detects, the game decides what happens.

  • Make a zone: create a box (builtin:cube) with visible: false, no collider, scaled to the area (a plate 2 × 0.2 × 2, a finish line 10 × 4 × 1), then systems_attach this system on it. A zone works hidden; the editor still shows it.
  • Per object (systems_set): detecte, who counts: joueur (default), personnages (the player and characters), objets (moving objects of the physique system), tout.
  • React in a script of the game: game.on("zone.entree", function(e) if e.cible == plate then ... end end). e.qui is who entered: game.player(), a character, or a moving object. A ball in a goal: the zone detects objets, and the script checks e.qui.
  • Something already inside when the game starts enters on the first step. game.set_solid(zone, false) switches a zone off; true switches it back on.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
The engine runs it once for the whole game: detecte = joueur sees every player, and zone.entree / zone.sortie carry joueur when a player enters or leaves.
